records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has taken any step to stop the illegal mining of sand from river banks;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) whether Government is planning to allow the import of sand for construction?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF MINES, COAL AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS <br/>(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI)<br/><br/>(a) & (b): Section 23C of the Mines and Minerals (Development & Regulation) (MMDR) Act, 1957, empowers the State Governments to make rules for preventing illegal mining, transportation and storage of minerals and for the purposes connected therewith. Sand is a minor mineral under Section 3(e) of the MMDR Act. For minor minerals, all policy and legislation for grant of mineral concessions, regulation and administration is covered in the jurisdiction of the State Governments under the MMDR Act and the Rules framed thereunder.<br/><br/>(c): As per the ITC (HS) Schedule-I (Import Policy), 2017, notified by Directorate General of Foreign Trade, import policy of natural sands all kinds is free. Therefore, the question of allowing / granting permission for import of sand for construction does not arise.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Creation of jobs with emergence of new technologies
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has identified new kind of jobs that may be created with the emergence of new technologies; <br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof;<br/>(c) 	whether Government plans to provide the required skill set to youth in this regard; and <br/>(d)	if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) to (d)	Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship is implementing flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) through National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC). NSDC is continually facilitating the development of Qualification Packs and National Occupational Standards (QP-NOS) in association with IT-ITeS SSC (NASSCOM) across emerging technologies influencing the Future of Work in India. The key areas addressed includes Cyber Security, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data Analytics (BDA), Cloud Computing, Block Chain, Robotic Process Automation (RPA), Internet of Things (IoT), Virtual Reality (VR), and Social and Mobile Applications. To enable the flexibility and mobility of the Indian Skilled workforce – NSDC is facilitating upskilling in tune with international frameworks and pathways.  <br/>Further, Director General of Training ,to keep pace with Technological innovations has also  introduced new trades  in the year 2018  viz. Geo-Informatics Assistant, Aeronautical Structure and Equipment Fitter, Additive Manufacturing Technician (3D Printing), Drone Pilot, Electrician Power Distribution, Technical Mechatronics, Solar Technician (Electrical), Internet of Things (Smart Agriculture, Smart Healthcare and Smart City), Soil Testing & Crop Management and Firemen etc. <br/>

Statements showing category-wise backlog reserved vacancies for the ten Ministries/Departments as on 01.01.2017 and 01.01.2018 is attached as Annexure-I and Annexure-II.<br/><br/> (b) and (c):  The Government undertakes steps from time to time to fill the backlog reserved vacancies including through special drives to reduce the vacancies.  <br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) the number of accidents on highways over the last three years, State-wise; and<br/><br/> (b) steps taken by Government to reduce the number of accidents on highways? <br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)<br/><br/>(a)	As per information received from police department of the State Governments, the total number of road accidents on National Highways and State Highways during the last three calendar years i.e. 2015 to 2017 is given below. <br/><br/>Year	Total number  of road accidents on NHs	Total number of road accidents on SHs<br/>2015	1,42,268	1,20,518<br/>2016	1,42,359	1,21,655<br/>2017	1,41,466	1,16,158<br/><br/>                      State-wise and year-wise break up of the same is given at annexure. <br/><br/>(b)	With regard to the steps taken by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to reduce  the  road accidents, details are as follows:<br/><br/>i.)	Advocacy/Publicity campaign on road safety through the electronic media and print media to create awareness. <br/> <br/>ii.)	Issue of Guidelines for protection of Good Samaritans.<br/><br/>iii.)	Setting up of model driving training Institutes in States.<br/><br/>iv.)	Sanction of 22 Inspection and certification Centres for testing the fitness of the commercial vehicles through an automated system. <br/><br/>v.)	Launch of mobile app for highway users i.e. “SukhadYatra 1033” which enables highways users to report potholes and other safety hazards on National Highways including accidents.<br/><br/>vi.)	Observance of Road Safety Week every calendar year for spreading awareness and strengthening road safety.<br/><br/>vii.)	The National Road Safety Policy outlines various policy measures such as promoting awareness, establishing road safety information data base, encouraging safer road infrastructure including application of intelligent transport, enforcement of safety laws. The Ministry has formulated a multi-pronged strategy to address the issue of road safety based on 4 ‘E’s viz. Education, Engineering (both of roads and vehicles), Enforcement and Emergency Care. Further, the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways has constituted a District Road Safety Committee in each district of the country to promote awareness amongst road users under the chairmanship of Hon’ble Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) from the district.<br/><br/>viii.)	Road safety has been made an integral part of road design at planning stage.  <br/><br/>ix.)	The threshold for four laning of national highway has been reduced from 15,000 Passenger Car Units (PCUs) to 10,000 PCUs.<br/><br/>x.)	Safety standards for automobiles have been improved.<br/> <br/>xi.)	High priority has been accorded to identification and rectification of black spots (accident prone spots) on national highways.<br/><br/>xii.)	Ministry has delegated powers to Regional Officers of MoRTH for technical approval to the detailed estimates for rectification of identified Road Accident black spots for expediting the rectification process to ensure safety of road users.<br/><br/>xiii.)	Guidelines for pedestrian facilities on National Highways for persons with disabilities have also been issued to all States / UTs.  <br/><br/>xiv.)	A Certification Course for Road Safety Auditors has been commenced in Indian Academy of Highway Engineers (IAHE) and 42 Auditors are certified. <br/><br/>xv.)	 Free Eye Check-up Camp and distribution of eye glasses is conducted for truck/bus drivers operating on NH.<br/><br/>xvi.)	Removal of Liquor Shops as per directions of Hon’ble Supreme Court vide circular of   F. No. RW/NH-33044/309/2016/S&R dated 06-04-2017 and 01-06-2017.<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Guidelines for establishment and maintenance of Old Age Homes
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) the details of the guidelines in place for establishment and maintenance of Old Age Homes in the country;<br/> <br/>(b) the number of Old Age Homes set up by Government in the country during the last three years; and <br/><br/>(c) the details of funds allocated by Government for setting up and maintaining Old Age Homes during the last three years?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT<br/>(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA)<br/><br/>(a):  This Ministry is implementing a Central Sector Scheme of Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSr.C) since 1992, under which grant in aid is given for running and maintenance of Senior Citizens Homes/ Continuous Care Homes/ Mobile Medicare Units etc. The main objective of the Scheme is to improve the quality of life of Older Persons by providing basic amenities like shelter, food, medical care and entertainment opportunities etc. Implementing Agencies (IAs) eligible for assistance under the Scheme are Panchayati Raj Institutions/Local Bodies, State Governments/UT Administrations through registered societies, Non-Government Organisations, Voluntary Organisations, Institutions or Organisations set up by Governments autonomous/subordinate bodies, Government Recognised Educational Institutions, Charitable Hospitals/Nursing Homes, and Recognised Youth Organisations such as Nehru Yuvak Kendra Sangathan (NYKS).    <br/><br/>(b) and (c) : This Ministry does not directly set up Old Age Homes. However, under the Scheme of Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSr.C), financial assistance in the form of grant in aid is given to the Implementing Agencies  for running and maintenance of, inter alia, Senior Citizens Homes etc. State wise details of project of Senior Citizens Homes supported and grant in aid released to the implementing agencies during last 3 years is at Annexure-I.<br/><br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Steps to improve indigenous technological development
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a)	the details of R&D expenditure over the last three years;<br/><br/>(b)	whether Government is aware that electronics imports are a measure of lack of technological self-sufficiency;<br/><br/>(c)	whether Government is taking any steps to improve indigenous technological development in terms of electronics; and<br/><br/>(d)	if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY, MINISTER OF EARTH SCIENCES AND MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE<br/>(DR. HARSH VARDHAN)<br/><br/>(a)	The R&D expenditure over the last three years for Ministry of Science and Technology is as follows:<br/><br/>Department	EXP 2016-17	EXP 2017-18	EXP 2018-19<br/>	PLAN	NON-PLAN		<br/>	(Rs. In Crores)<br/>DST	3835.33	490.26	4635.22	5043.68<br/>DSIR	2287.83	1763.84	4618.61	4568.45<br/>DBT	1874.60	20.90	2231.42	2379.10<br/>TOTAL	7997.76	2275.00	11485.25	11991.24<br/><br/>(b) to (d):   Steps taken by the Government for promotion of domestic electronics manufacturing through Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY):-<br/><br/>(i)	Modified Special Incentive Package Scheme (M-SIPS) provides financial incentives to offset disability and attract investments in the electronics manufacturing sector. The scheme was open to receive applications till 31.12.2018 for new projects as well as expansion projects.<br/>(ii)	The Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC) Scheme was notified to provide financial support for creation of state-of-art infrastructure for electronics manufacturing units. The scheme was open for receipt of application for a period of 5 years, i.e., upto 21.10.2017. Further period of 5 years is available for disbursement of funds for the approved applicants. Under the scheme, approval has been accorded for setting up of 20 Greenfield EMCs and 3 Common Facility Centres (CFCs) in 15 States across the country. <br/>(iii)	Tariff Structure has been rationalized to promote domestic manufacturing of electronic goods, including, inter-alia, Cellular mobile handsets, Televisions, Electronic components, Set Top Boxes for TV, LED products and Medical electronics equipment. To promote domestic value addition in mobile handsets and their parts/ components manufacturing, a Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP) has been notified. As a result, India has rapidly started attracting investments into this sector and significant manufacturing capacities have been set up in the country during the past four years. The manufacturing of mobile handsets and their parts/ components has been steadily moving from Semi Knocked Down (SKD) to Completely Knocked Down (CKD) level, thereby progressively increasing the domestic value addition.  <br/>(iv)	As per extant Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) policy, FDI upto 100% under the automatic route is permitted for electronics manufacturing, subject to applicable laws/ regulations; security and other conditionalities.<br/>(v)	For promotion of exports in the sector, Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS) and Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Scheme are available under the Foreign Trade Policy, 2015-20. MEIS offers export incentives so as to offset disabilities of manufacturing. Zero duty EPCG scheme allows import of capital goods at zero customs duty, subject to specified export obligation.    <br/>(vi)	The import of used plant and machinery having a residual life of at least 5 years for use by the electronics manufacturing industry has been simplified through the amendment of Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, vide Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change Notification dated 11.06.2018.  <br/>(vii)	Notified capital goods for manufacture of specified electronic goods are permitted for import at “Nil” Basic Customs Duty.<br/>(viii)	The Department of Revenue vide Notification No.60/2018-Customs dated 11.09.2018 has amended the Notification No.158/95-Customs dated 14.11.1995, relaxing the ageing restriction from 3 years to 7 years for specified electronic goods manufactured in India and re-imported into India for repairs or reconditioning. <br/>(ix)	In order to ensure safety of Indian citizens by curbing import of substandard and unsafe electronic goods into India, MeitY has notified “Electronics and Information Technology Goods (Requirement of Compulsory Registration) Order, 2012” for mandatory compliance. As per the provisions of the order, the manufacturer has to get the product tested in laboratories recognized by Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), take registration from BIS and put the registration mark on the product. 44 product categories have been notified under the order.  <br/>(x)	The National Policy on Electronics 2019 (NPE 2019) has been notified on 25.02.2019. The vision of  NPE 2019 is to position India as a global hub for Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) by encouraging and driving capabilities in the country for developing core components, including chipsets, and creating an enabling environment for the industry to compete globally.<br/>(xi)	 Electronics Development Fund (EDF) has been set up as a “Fund of Funds” to participate in professionally managed “Daughter Funds” which in turn will provide risk capital to companies developing new technologies in the area of electronics, nano-electronics and Information Technology (IT). This fund is expected to foster R&D and innovation in these technology sectors.<br/>(xii)	Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) provides grant-in-aid support to institutes of higher learning like IITs, IISc, Central Universities and R&D Organizations to conduct research in identified thrust areas. These research programmes are aimed to deliver proof of concept, technology/ product development and transfer of technology. These research programmes also result in generation of specialized manpower to support “Make in India”.  <br/>(xiii)	Indian Conditional Access System (iCAS) has been developed in Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode to promote indigenous manufacturing of Set Top Boxes (STBs). The implementation of iCAS in the cable networks is underway.<br/>(xiv)	An Electropreneur park has been set up in New Delhi for providing incubation for development of ESDM sector which will contribute IP creation and Product Development in the sector.<br/>(xv)	National Centre of Excellence in Large Area Flexible Electronics (NCFLEX) has been set up in IIT-Kanpur with the objectives to promote R&D; Manufacturing; Ecosystem; Entrepreneurship; International Partnerships and Human Resources and develop prototypes in collaboration with industry for commercialization. <br/>(xvi)	National Centre of Excellence for Technology on Internal Security (NCETIS) has been set up at IIT-Bombay with the objective to address the internal security needs of the nation on continuous basis by delivering technology prototypes required for internal security and to promote domestic industry in internal security. <br/>(xvii)	Centre for Excellence on Internet of Things (IoT) has been set up in Bengaluru, jointly with NASSCOM. <br/>(xviii)	An Incubation centre with focus on medical electronics has been set up at IIT-Patna. A fabless chip design incubation centre has been set up in IIT Hyderabad to incubate start-ups in semiconductor design and to provide one-stop service to start-ups intending to enter this space. <br/>(xix)	A  Centre of Excellence (CoE) on FinTech at STPI Chennai has been set up to provide infrastructure, resources, coaching/ mentorship, technology support and funding to emerging start-ups in the FinTech sector through a collaborative approach including M/s intellect design as industrial partner, NPCI, UIDAI and Partner Banks as Yes Bank, PayPal, HSBC, IIT Chennai as knowledge partner and TiE Chennai to provide industrial connect.<br/>(xx)	An IoT OpenLab - a Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Internet of Things in partnership with Arrow Electronics at STPI Bangalore has been set up to provide academic and business mentoring of the startups in the IoT emerging technology area for developing products and/ or services around IoT.<br/>(xxi)	An ESDM Incubation Centre has been set up at Bhubaneswar with the objective of creating a holistic eco-system to promote ESDM innovation, R&D and create Indian intellectual property in the eastern region of the country.<br/><br/>Ministry of Science and Technology is also supporting Research and Innovation for application of electronics in specified areas by providing funding support to scientists, researchers, start ups and industries.<br/><br/>                       ********<br/>

records.qtitle: Vacancies for doctors and nurses at PHCs
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) the State-wise details of the number of vacancies for doctors and nurses at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), over the last three years;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government has taken steps to ensure doctors and nurses at PHCs are adequately trained; and<br/><br/>(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a):	As per Rural Health Statistics (RHS), the State/UT wise status of availability of doctors and nurses at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), and vacancies thereof over last three year is given at Annexure.    <br/><br/>(b) & (c):	Public health being a State subject, the primary responsibility to ensure adequate training for doctors and nurses at PHCs, lies with the State Governments. Under National Health Mission (NHM), financial and technical support is provided to States/UTs to strengthen their healthcare systems including support for training of doctors and Nurses in service delivery and management through appropriately designed training programmes, based on the requirements posed by them in their Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) within their overall resource envelope.<br/>               <br/>Further, the Government has taken various steps to train more health professionals and depute them in rural areas, these efforts include:<br/>I.	50% of the seats in Post Graduate Diploma Courses are reserved for Medical Officers in the Government service, who have served for at least three years in remote and difficult areas. After acquiring the PG Diploma, the Medical Officers has to serve for two more years in remote and/or difficult   areas and/or rural areas.<br/><br/>II.	Incentive at the rate of 10% of the marks obtained for each year in service in remote and/or difficult or rural areas as upto the maximum of 30% of the marks obtained in the entrance test for admissions in Post Graduate Medical Courses.   <br/><br/><br/>III.	Support is provided to States/UTs for hard area allowance to doctors for serving in rural and remote areas and for their residential quarters so that they find it attractive to serve in public health facilities in such areas.<br/><br/>IV.	Enhancement of maximum intake capacity at MBBS level from 150 to 250.<br/><br/>V.	Relaxation in the norms of setting up of Medical College in terms of requirement for land, faculty, staff, bed/bed strength and other infrastructure.<br/><br/>VI.	Establishment of New Medical Colleges by upgrading district/referral hospitals preferably in underserved districts of the country.<br/><br/>VII.	Strengthening/ upgradation of existing State Government/Central Government Medical Colleges to increase MBBS seats.<br/><br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Sports infrastructure and facilities in schools and colleges
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government is aware of the poor sports infrastructure and facilities in schools and colleges across the country;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the steps taken by Government to improve the sports infrastructure in schools and colleges over the last three years; and<br/><br/>(c) details of expenditure on providing or improving sports infrastructure in schools and colleges over the last three years?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>FOR YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS<br/>{SHRI KIREN RIJIJU}<br/><br/>(a) to (c) ‘Sports’ being a State subject the responsibility for providing sports infrastructure, including in Schools and Colleges across the country, rests with State/Union Territory Governments. Central Government supplements efforts of the State/Union Territory Governments for bridging critical gaps in sports infrastructure. Information regarding projects sanctioned for sports infrastructure in Schools/ Colleges/ Universities in the last three years under Khelo India Scheme is at Annexure.<br/>****

records.qn_text: (a)	steps taken by Government to improve credit worthiness of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises during the last three years;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether Government plans to reduce infrastructure gaps for the MSME sector; and<br/><br/>(c) 	if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?  <br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES<br/>(SHRI NITIN GADKARI) <br/><br/>(a):  The Ministry of MSME implements various schemes and programmes like Credit Guarantee Scheme, Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme, MSE-Cluster Development Programme, Marketing Development Assistance Scheme, National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme, Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme etc. These schemes address various aspects of the MSME development including promotion of access to credit & infrastructure.<br/><br/>(b) & (c):      The MSE Cluster Development Programme of the Ministry of MSME addresses the needs of common infrastructure for MSEs. The programme supports creation & upgradation of industrial estates and setting up of Common Facility Centres. <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Financial reporting system for local Governments
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has put in place a credible financial reporting system for local Governments;<br/>(b) if so, the details of reporting in the last five years, State-wise; and<br/>(c) if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ<br/><br/>(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR)<br/><br/>(a), (b) & (c): 	Yes Sir. ‘Panchayat’ is a state subject and it is the primary responsibility of the States to provide for systems for administering Panchayats. However, the Government is implementing PRIASoft, a web based accounting application for better financial reporting and management, under e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) for Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). It aims to keep track of all the in-flow (Receipts) and out- flow (Expenditure). <br/>The State-wise details of the reporting in the last five years are given at Annexure I.<br/>*****<br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: to state the number and details of social science institutes and departments, engineering and medical colleges set up by Government during the last three years, State-wise?
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI RAMESH POKHRIYAL ‘NISHANK’)<br/><br/>The Government does not set up social science departments, as these departments are set up in the university system. Although, the Government has not set up any social science institute during the last three years, however, to promote research in the social sciences, the Department of Higher Education, MHRD through the Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), in August, 2018 has launched a Scheme: Impactful Policy Research in Social Science (IMPRESS), at a total cost of Rs. 414 Crore to support research in the social sciences in higher educational institutions.<br/>Further, as per the information given by All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the Government has set up 78 engineering colleges and 50 medical colleges respectively during the last three years and State-wise details of which are given at Annexure.<br/>*****

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a)the details of labour reforms undertaken by Government during the last three years;<br/> (b)whether Government plans to undertake any new labour reforms; and<br/> (c)if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (IC) FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT<br/>(SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR)<br/><br/>(a):		 The labour reforms undertaken by Government during the last three years are as follows:- <br/>?	Payment of Wages (Amendment) Act, 2017 enabling payment of Wages to employees by Cash or Cheque or crediting it to their bank account.<br/>?	Maternity Benefit Amendment Act, 2017, increases the paid maternity leave from 12 weeks to 26 weeks.<br/>?	The Employee Compensation (Amendment) Act, seeks to rationalize penalties and strengthen the rights of the workers under the Act.<br/>?	The Payment of Gratuity (Amendment) Act, 2018, provides flexibility to the Central Government to increase the ceiling limit of gratuity to such amount as may be notified from time to time.  The ceiling limit of gratuity has been increased from Rs. 10 Lakh to 20 Lakh vide Notification dated 29th March, 2018.<br/>Contd..2/-<br/><br/>::  2  ::<br/><br/>?	Ministry has notified “Ease of Compliance to maintain Registers under various Labour Laws Rules, 2017” on 21st February 2017 which has in effect replaced the 56 Registers/Forms under 9 Central Labour Laws into 5 common Registers/Forms. Further, the number of forms provided under 3 Central Acts/Rules has been reduced from existing 44 to 14.<br/>?	Under Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, the category i.e. Fixed Term Employment, with all Statutory Benefits, has been extended to all Sectors to impart flexibility to an establishment to employ people to meet the fluctuating demands, vide the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Central (Amendment) Rules, 2018.<br/><br/>(b) & (c):	 The Second National Commission on Labour has recommended that the existing Labour Laws should be broadly grouped into four or five Labour Codes on functional basis. Accordingly, the Ministry has taken steps for drafting four Labour Codes on Wages; Industrial Relations; Social Security; and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions respectively, by simplifying, amalgamating and rationalizing the relevant provisions of the existing Central Labour Laws. <br/><br/>The 4 draft Labour Codes are at pre-legislative stage.<br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) the State-wise details of number of mob lynchings that took place over the last three years;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government plans to address the mob violence and lynching in the country; and<br/><br/>(c) if so, the details of steps taken by Government to address this issue?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI NITYANAND RAI)<br/><br/>(a) to (c):   ‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India and State Governments are responsible for prevention, detection, registration and investigation of crime and for prosecuting the criminals through their law enforcement agencies. The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) does not maintain specific data with respect to lynching incidents in the country. The Ministry of Home Affairs have issued advisories to States and UTs, from time to time, to maintain law and  order  and  ensure  that <br/><br/><br/>-2-<br/>R.S.US.Q.NO.521 FOR 26.06.2019<br/><br/>any person who takes law into his/her own hand is punished promptly as per law. The Ministry of Home Affairs have issued an advisory on 09.08.2016 to all States/UTs for taking prompt and strict action against miscreants who take law into their own hands.  An advisory dated 04.07.2018 was issued to the States and UTs wherein they were advised to keep watch on circulation of fake news and rumours having potential of inciting violence, take all required measures to counter them effectively and to deal firmly with persons taking law into their own hands. Further, advisories dated 23.07.2018 and 25.09.2018 were issued to the State Governments/UT Administrations for taking measures to curb incidents of mob lynching in the country. Government through audio-visual media has also generated public awareness in this regard. Government has also sensitized the service providers to take steps to check the propagation of false news and rumours having potential to incite mob violence.<br/> <br/>********<br/><br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: <br/><br/><br/>(a) the details of the number of Primary Health Care Centres (PHCs) in the country, State-wise; <br/><br/>(b) whether Government has conducted any review or audit of the PHCs recently and if so, the details and results thereof; and <br/><br/>(c) the details of the steps being taken by Government to upgrade PHCs in the country in order to achieve the goal of healthcare for all?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE <br/>(DR. HARSH VARDHAN)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA<br/>STARRED QUESTION NO. 42* FOR 25TH JUNE, 2019<br/><br/>(a)	The details of the number of Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in the country, State/UT-wise, as per data uploaded by States/UTs on Health Management Information System (HMIS) portal, as on May 2019, are placed at Annexure-I.<br/><br/>(b)	The Government has a system of PHC Grading through which PHCs are monitored periodically.  Grading of PHC is done based on the information uploaded by States/UTs on the HMIS portal. The details of the State/UT-wise number of PHCs graded on a scale of 0-5 and NE(Not Eligible)is placed at Annexure II.  <br/><br/>(c)	As per the budget announcement 2017-18, 1,50,000 Health Sub Centres and Primary Health Centres are to be transformed into Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs) by  December, 2022 to provide Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC) to ensure health for all.<br/> <br/>Under Ayushman Bharat-HWC, CPHC includes promotive, preventive, curative, palliative and rehabilitative services. The AB-HWCs are envisioned to provide an expanded      range of services to include care for non-communicable diseases, palliative and rehabilitative care, Oral, Eye and ENT care, mental health and first level care for emergencies and trauma as well as health promotion and wellness activities like Yoga apart from services already being provided for Maternal and Child Health including immunization and communicable diseases. Free essential drugs and diagnostic services are also being provisioned through these HWCs.<br/> <br/>As on 17th June 2019, 19,282 AB-HWCs are operational in the Country providing comprehensive primary health care which includes 11864 PHCs.<br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) the details of the number of wellness centres that have been established by Government in the past three years, State wise;<br/><br/>(b) the details of the standards prescribed by Government for establishing these wellness centres; and<br/><br/>(c) the details of the number of beneficiaries for each wellness centre, State-wise?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a):	As per the budget announcement 2017-18, 1.5 lakh Health Sub Centres and Primary Health Centres are being transformed into Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs) for provision of comprehensive primary care that includes preventive and promotive care at the community level with continuum of care approach across the country for all population. The roll out plan of Ayushman Bharat - HWCs is given as below:<br/>•	FY 2018-19 = 15,000<br/>•	FY 2019-20 = 25,000 (Cumulative 40,000)<br/>•	FY 2020-21 = 30,000 (Cumulative 70,000)<br/>•	FY 2021-2022 = 40,000 (Cumulative 1,10,000)<br/>•	Till 31st December 2022 = 40,000 (Cumulative 1,50,000)<br/><br/>So far, approvals for 52,744 Ayushman Bharat - Health and Wellness Centres (AB-HWCs) have been accorded. The state-wise details of 19,282 operational Ayushman Bharat- Health & Wellness Centres (AB-HWCs) as on 17.06.2019 is furnished at Annexure.<br/><br/>(b):	The Ayushman Bharat Operational Guidelines for Comprehensive Primary Healthcare (CPHC) through HWCs have been developed and disseminated to all States/UTs. The guidelines provide details on key essential inputs for operationalizing a AB-HWC that include Primary Healthcare Team, Logistics (drugs and diagnosis), Infrastructure strengthening (including Branding), Capacity building, Health Promotion and Community mobilization.<br/><br/>The Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) for AB-HWCs are being developed to meet the norms specified in the Operational Guidelines of Ayushman Bharat-CPHC through HWCs.<br/><br/>(c):	Services at AB-HWCs are free and universal to all individuals residing in the      service area.<br/>

records.ans_text: Minister of State in the Ministry of External Affairs; and Minister of State in the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs<br/>(Shri V. Muraleedharan)<br/><br/>(a to b) The information is given at Annexure-‘A’.<br/><br/>(c)	Information has to be collected from various sources like other Ministries/Departments of Government of India, State Governments and other agencies. Non furnishing of such information timely results in  pendency.<br/><br/>(d)	Ministries are reminded from time to time to collect information expeditiously and fulfill  the assurances.<br/>

records.qtitle: Interlinking of Cauvery river across Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government plans to undertake any initiative to interlink and nationalize rivers in the country; <br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and <br/>(c) whether Government plans to interlink the Cauvery river across the States of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka and if so, the details thereof''?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI & SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT<br/><br/>(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA)<br/><br/>(a) & (b)	The National Perspective Plan (NPP) was prepared by the then Ministry of Irrigation (now Ministry of Jal Shakti) in August 1980 for water resources development through inter basin transfer of water, for transferring water from water surplus basins to water-deficit basins. Under the NPP, the National Water Development Agency (NWDA) has identified 30 links (16 under Peninsular Component & 14 under Himalayan Component) for preparation of Feasibility Reports (FRs). The details of above river linking projects viz., rivers, States concerned is given at Annexure. <br/><br/>      No proposal is under consideration of the Central Government for nationalization of the rivers. <br/><br/>(c)	   Under the Peninsular Component of NPP, Mahanadi-Godavari-Krishna-Pennar-Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar linking scheme has been identified as the Nine link system. Mahanadi-Godavari is the mother link of this system. records.qtitle: Mechanization of agricultural production and new farming techniques
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a)	 the details of funds allocated by Government for boosting mechanization of agricultural production processes, State-wise; <br/><br/>(b)	 the details of the initiatives taken by Government in this regard; and <br/><br/>(c)	 the manner in which Government imparts knowledge to farmers regarding usage of new farming techniques?	<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE <br/><br/>(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR)<br/><br/>(a):	To promote the Farm Mechanization in the country, Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare has introduced a dedicated Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) w.e.f. 2014-15 .<br/>       <br/>Under the above Scheme financial assistance is provided to farmers through State Governments for purchase of various agricultural implements.<br/>    <br/>A special Scheme to support the efforts of the Governments of Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and the NCT of Delhi to address air pollution due to stubble burning and to subsidize machinery for the farmers for in-situ management of crop residue, a new Central Sector Scheme on ‘Promotion of Agricultural Mechanization for In-Situ Management of Crop Residue in the States of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and NCT of Delhi” (CRM) for the period from 2018-19 to 2019-20 has been also launched.<br/>    <br/>  The farm mechanization component is also available under various schemes like Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) , National Food Security Mission (NFSM)  and National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm (NMOOP) and Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY).<br/>      <br/>The details of State-wise funds released under SMAM , CRM, MIDH , NFSM and NMOOP is enclosed as an Annexure-I , II , III , IV and  V respectively.<br/>      <br/>  The details of State-wise number of agricultural mechanization related project sanctioned and cost of the its projects under RKVY is enclosed at Annexure VI.<br/>Contd..2/-<br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/> 	    Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is also providing funds to their All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) and also to State Agricultural Universities (SAU) . The State wise funds allocated by ICAR is enclosed at Annexure VII.<br/><br/>(b):	 Under SMAM , lot of initiatives are taken by Government for boosting mechanization. The SMAM scheme aims at ‘reaching the unreached’ by giving more focus to the small and marginal farmers, Promoting ‘Custom Hiring Centers’, creating hubs for hi-tech & high value farm equipments especially in the regions where availability of farm power is low, creating awareness among stakeholders through demonstration and capacity building activities, and ensuring performance- testing and certification at designated testing centers located all over the country. <br/><br/>          During the period 2014-15 to 2018-19 as an Government’s initiatives under agricultural mechanization, under SMAM scheme, total 58303 numbers of demonstrations conducted , 40033 numbers of trainees trained , 962528 numbers of various agricultural machinery distributed and 13899 numbers of Custom Hiring Centers established and during 2018-19 under CRM scheme, demonstrations conducted in 18555 acres area, 22525 numbers of trainees trained , 32831 numbers of various agricultural machinery distributed and 7444 numbers of Custom Hiring Centers established.<br/><br/>(c):	     Government has introduced and formulated various schemes to promote the use of modern farming techniques in agriculture in the country which are as below.<br/><br/>(i)   Sub Mission on Agricultural Extension (SMAE)<br/>(ii)  Sub-Mission on Seed and Planting Material (SMSP) <br/>(iii)  Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) <br/>(iv)  Sub Mission on Plant Protection and Plant Quarantine (SMPP)<br/>(v )  National Food Security Mission (NFSM)<br/>(vi)  National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm (NMOOP)<br/>(vii)  Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)<br/>(viii) National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture(NMSA)<br/>(ix)   Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana - Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture and Allied sector Rejuvenation (RKVY-RAFTAAR)<br/>     <br/> These schemes are supporting various farm technologies to sustain growth of agriculture such as integrated farming system/ cropping system with appropriate resource conservation technologies; development of high yielding pest/ disease tolerant crop varieties/ hybrids; water use efficiency enhancement through micro irrigation; soil test based balanced and judicious use of fertilizers; dissemination of agriculture related information to the farming community through various ICT enabled delivery channels including SMSs, internet kiosks, farmers portals etc; scientific storage of both perishable and non-perishable produce; precision farming; increasing the reach of farm mechanization by promoting “Custom Hiring Centres”, creating hubs for hi-tech & high value farm equipments; promotion of latest technologies on crops specific cultivation; protected cultivation of horticultural products, organic farming etc.<br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the Government has identified the immense potential of apprenticeship training at Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) across the country;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, whether Government has taken steps to boost apprenticeship training by involving all the stakeholders including the State Government and the private industry; and <br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details therefor and if not, the reason therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a)	Yes Sir.Government has pre-approved all the Government and Private ITIs having rating 2.0 and above as basic training provider, so that fresher apprentices can acquire a reasonable ability to handle Instruments/Machineries/Equipment independently prior to moving to Shop Floor/Work Area for practical training / On-Job Training under National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme under Apprentices Act, 1961.<br/><br/>(b)	Yes Sir. Government has taken several steps to boost apprenticeship training by involving all the stakeholders including the State Government and the private industry.<br/><br/>(c)	Details are annexed as Annexure -1.<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>Annexure-1<br/><br/>ANNEX REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARA (c) of RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1223 DUE FOR REPLY ON 13.02.19.<br/><br/>Details as follows:<br/><br/>1.	A fully dedicated portal for apprenticeship training is prepared and made functional.<br/>2.	Comprehensive changes brought under Guidelines for National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), Basic Training Provider (BTP), Third Party Aggregators (TPAs) and framing of courses under apprenticeship training program.<br/>3.	Industry representative appointed as Brand Ambassadors for promotion and creating awareness among the all stakeholders for apprenticeship training.<br/>4.	Awareness meeting, seminars and campaign conducted in industry clusters throughout the country.<br/>5.	For strengthening apprenticeship training at State Government level, funds released to create State Apprenticeship monitoring cell (SAMC).<br/>6.	For promotion of apprenticeship training, State Governments asked to use different advertising methods like hoarding, pamphlets, newspapers etc.<br/>7.	A television series called “Hunarbaaz” telecasted nationwide for creating awareness for apprenticeship training scheme.<br/>8.	Under the World Bank aided project called STRIVE, Industry Apprenticeship Initiative in industry clusters has been initiated.<br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) 	the details of financial incentive schemes provided to startup companies in the sector of micro, small and medium enterprises in the country;<br/><br/>(b) 	 the State-wise details of the finances disbursed to sartups during the last three years and current year; and<br/> <br/>(c) 	the details of the incubation centres established by Government to promote sartups?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES<br/>(SHRI GIRIRAJ SINGH)<br/><br/> (a): 	The Start-Up India initiative aims to build a strong eco-system for nurturing innovation and startups in the country.  Various financial incentives provided for Startup Companies under the Startup India initiative include providing funding support through a Fund of Funds, Credit Guarantee Fund for Startups, tax exemption on Capital Gains, tax exemption for initial 3 years, and allowing external commercial borrowing up to US $ 3 million or equivalent per financial year.<br/><br/>(b): 	Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) implements Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) for providing financial assistance to set up new enterprises.  PMEGP is a major credit-linked subsidy programme aimed at generating self-employment opportunities through establishment of micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector by helping traditional artisans and unemployed youth. The state wise details of the finance disbursed under the PMEGP are at Annexure-I.<br/><br/>(c):  Ministry of MSME implemented the Scheme namely Support for Entrepreneurial and Managerial Development of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) through Incubators. Under the Scheme, Government of India provided opportunity to the innovators to develop and nurture their innovative ideas. <br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has taken any action to ensure implementation of the USTTAD Scheme to upgrade skills and training in traditional arts and crafts for development of minorities;<br/>(b) if so, the details of the funds allocated and utilised in Tamil Nadu; and <br/>(c) whether Government has set up any mechanism to monitor the utilisation of these funds by the State Governments and if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS<br/> (SHRI MUKHTAR ABBAS NAQVI)<br/><br/><br/>(a):  Yes, Sir.<br/>(b): Upgrading the Skills and Training in Traditional Arts/ Crafts for Development (USTTAD) scheme has been launched on 14th May, 2015 to preserve the rich heritage of traditional arts/crafts of minorities. The scheme aims at capacity building and updating the traditional skills of master craftsmen/artisans; documentation of identified traditional arts/crafts of minorities; set standards for traditional skills; training of minority youths in various identified traditional arts/crafts through master craftsmen; and develop national and international market linkages. Scheme is implemented through selected Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) in the States on the basis of their proposals. So far, no PIAs have been empanelled from Tamilnadu in this scheme. <br/>(c): The scheme’s guidelines provide for monitoring and inspection of the project. State Government/MAEF Inspector and officials of the Ministry are also assigned to monitor/inspect the projects from time to time. <br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Educational advancement of religious minorities in Tamil Nadu
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: a) the steps taken by Government in the last three years and current year<br/>to ensure an increase in educational and employment opportunities for<br/>religious minorities in the State of Tamil Nadu;<br/>(b) whether Government provides any scholarship for minority students till<br/>the university level; and<br/>(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI MUKHTAR ABBAS NAQVI)<br/>(a) to (c): The Ministry of Minority Affairs implements fifteen Schemes throughout<br/>the country (including Tamil Nadu), for educational and economic empowerment<br/>of six Centrally notified minority communities namely Muslim, Christian, Sikh,<br/>Buddhist, Jain and Parsi (Zoroastrians). The schemes are as under:<br/>(i) Pre-matric Scholarship Scheme (for students of Class I to X);<br/>(ii) Post-matric Scholarship Scheme (for students of Class XI to Ph.D.);<br/>(iii) Merit-cum Means based Scholarship Scheme (For students of<br/>Professional and Technical courses at Under Graduate and Post<br/>Graduate level);<br/>(iv) Maulana Azad National Fellowship (MANF) (for M.Phil & Ph.D);<br/>(v) Free Coaching & Allied Scheme (for Competitive Examinations of<br/>Professional Courses and Government jobs);<br/>(vi) Support for Minorities (for clearing prelims exam conducted by Union<br/>Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC)<br/>and State Public Service Commissions (SPSCs));<br/>(vii) Padho Pardesh (for overseas studies at Masters, M.Phil. and Ph.D.<br/>Level);<br/>(viii) Nai Manzil - A scheme to provide education and skill training to the<br/>youth from Minority communities. Provide education bridge program<br/>to eligible minority youth, to obtain open schooling certification of<br/>class 8th / 10th. Impart high quality skill training including soft skills<br/>leading to productive employment. Provide job placement support to<br/>assist sustainable employment to those students who opt to the labour<br/>market;<br/>(ix) Begam Hajrat Mahal National Scholarship for Meritorious Girls<br/>belonging to Minorities- Implemented by Maulana Azad Education<br/>Foundation (MAEF) (for minority girls studying in Class XIth and XIIth<br/>Standard).<br/>(x) Seekho aur Kamao –Seekho aur Kamao is a placement linked skill<br/>development scheme that aims at upgrading the skills of minority<br/>youth in various modern/traditional skills depending upon their<br/>qualification, present economic trends and market potential, which<br/>can earn them a suitable employment or make them suitably skilled to<br/>go for self-employment.<br/>(xi) USTTAD - The scheme “Upgrading the Skills and Training in<br/>Traditional Arts/Crafts for Development (USTTAD)” aims at capacity<br/>building and updating the traditional skills of master<br/>craftsmen/artisans; documentation of identified traditional arts/crafts<br/>of minorities; set standards for traditional skills; training of minority<br/>youths in various identified traditional arts/crafts through master<br/>craftsmen; and develop national and international market linkages.<br/>Hunar Haat is also being organised under this Scheme from 2016-17<br/>to further promote traditional crafts/arts, employment generation and<br/>strengthen their market linkages.<br/>(xii) Nai Roshni – The scheme for leadership development of Minority<br/>Women. Under this scheme, a new component of economic<br/>empowerment is implemented for.<br/>(xiii) Gharib Nawaz Skill Development Training for Minorities – A scheme to<br/>provide short-term job oriented skill development courses to youths<br/>belonging to the 06 centrally notified minority communities, namely,<br/>Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains {implemented<br/>through Maulana Azad Education Foundation (MAEF)}.<br/>(xiv) Bridge Course for madarsa students & school dropouts by Aligarh<br/>Muslim University, Aligarh and Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi under<br/>Nai Manzil scheme (implemented through MAEF).<br/>(xv) Concessional credit through National Minorities Development and<br/>Finance Corporation (NMDFC).<br/>The details of all these schemes are available on the website of this Ministry i.e.<br/>www.minorityaffairs.gov.in / www.maef.nic.in / www.nmdfc.org.<br/>*****

records.qtitle: Discrimination against differentlyabled persons under MGNREGA
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government is aware that differently-abled persons continue to experience 	discrimination under MGNREGA scheme; <br/><br/>(b)	whether the number of differently-abled persons employed under the MGNREGA scheme has increased in the last year and if so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(c)	details of steps being taken by Government, particularly in the State of Tamil Nadu, to increase the participation of differently-abled persons in employment activities in the rural areas?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI RAM KRIPAL YADAV)<br/><br/>(a)& (b):	The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), 2005 provides at least one hundred days of guaranteed wage employment in every financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. The details of number of differently-abled persons worked under the MGNREGA during the last three financial years and current financial year 2018-19 (as on 06.02.2019) is given below:<br/><br/>                                          (in lakh)<br/>Financial Years	 2015-16  2016-17  2017-18   2018-19 (as on <br/>                                                 06.02.2019)<br/><br/>Differently<br/>abled persons<br/>worked	          4.60	    4.72     4.72	 4.25<br/><br/>(c):	State Governments including Tamil Nadu have been advised to take the following steps for increasing the participation of differently-abled persons under MGNREGA:<br/><br/>(i)	states to identify specific works which can be done by differently-abled persons;<br/><br/>(ii)	differently-abled persons can be grouped together as a fixed group to accomplish the works proposed for them;<br/><br/>(iii)	differently abled persons should be given preference for appointment as Mates for MGNREGA works and as workers for providing drinking water, to manage crèches etc., at the work site.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has taken steps to ensure that all land and environmental clearances are obtained before awarding highway projects to concessionaires;<br/><br/>(b) if not, the reasons therefor;<br/><br/>(c) whether Government is taking any step to establish a dispute redressal mechanism for clearing stressed or delayed road projects; and<br/><br/>(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? <br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>         (SHRI MANSUKH L. MANDAVIYA)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) The process of awarding the contract involves various stages which includes appointment of consultant for DPR preparation, finalization of DPRs, appraisal of the project by the Competent Authorities, invitation of bids and finalization of successful bidders. Further, the projects are awarded based on the preparedness in terms of pre-construction activities mainly in land acquisition.  As per current stipulation, projects are appraised by the Competent Authority after 3D is notified for a substantial portion of land and compensation award is declared for majority of the acquired land. Also, as per Concession Agreement, 80 % of the land in respect of BOT projects and 90 percent of the length for EPC projects should be available for declaration of the appointed date.<br/>As a consequence of the MoEF modified guidelines and also the modification of criteria for obtaining environment clearance, there is no longer a requirement of Environment Clearance (EC) for a large number of projects. <br/><br/>(c) & (d) Following the decisions of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) and the provisions contained in the Arbitration & Conciliation Act 1996, with the approval of NHAI Board, two nos. of Conciliation Committee of Independent Experts (CCIE-1 & CCIE -2) have been constituted. Till date 19 cases have been referred to and dealt by CCIE, out of which 6 conciliation failed, 8 succeeded and 5 are ongoing.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a)	 whether Government is setting up an old age pension scheme for farmers over the age of 60 years, if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b)	 whether Government plans to provide for alternate source of income for such farmers who are too old for agricultural labour; and<br/><br/>(c)	 if so, the details thereof?	<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE <br/><br/>(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA)<br/><br/>(a):     There are various welfare Schemes/ programmes being implemented by the Government which, among others, cover people above 60 year of age including farmers. These include Atal Pension Yojana(APY), Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY), Indira Gandhi Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Integrated Programme of Older Persons (IPOP), Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY), Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) and Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY).<br/> <br/>(b) & (c):     The Government with a view to augment the income of Small and Marginal Farmers, in the Union Budget 2019 has announced “Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAmman Nidhi (PM-KiSaN)” a new Central Sector Scheme will be 100% funded by the Government of India.<br/><br/>Under the Scheme, financial benefit of Rs. 6000/- per year will be provided to all Small and Marginal Farmer families having cultivable land holding upto 2 hectare. This financial benefit will be provided in 3 equal installments of Rs. 2000/- each in a period of every four months in a financial year. The benefit shall be admissible under the scheme w.e.f. 01.12.2018. The definition of a Small and Marginal landholder farmer family is comprising husband, wife and minor children who collectively own cultivable land upto 2 hectare as per land records of the concerned State/UT. Thus, a farmer, irrespective of age can avail this benefit of income  support provided that his/her family is of small and marginal category and eligible as per the scheme guidelines. 	<br/><br/>**********<br/>

records.qtitle: Occupational exposure of farmers to pesticides
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether there have been farmers’ deaths due to occupational exposure to pesticides in the last four years and the current year in the State of Tamil Nadu; <br/><br/>(b)	 if so, the details of the common pesticides involved in these cases; and <br/><br/>(c) 	whether the Ministry plans to ban or prohibit the use of these pesticides by farmers to protect public health?<br/>	<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE<br/><br/>(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	 As informed by the State Government of Tamil Nadu, the details of farmer’s death due to occupational exposure to pesticides in the last four years and the current year are as follows:<br/><br/>S.No. 	Year 	Number of Deaths <br/>1	2014-15	Nil <br/>2	2015-16	Nil <br/>3	2016-17	Nil <br/>4	2017-18 	4<br/>5	2018-19 <br/>(up to 31.1.2019)	Nil <br/><br/>Use of unapproved combinations of pesticides such as Monocrotophos 36% SL, Profenophos 50% EC & Acephate 75% SP were involved in the above mentioned deaths.  <br/><br/>(c):	 The Registration Committee, constituted under Section 5 of the Insecticides Act, 1968 registers pesticides after considering its efficacy and safety to human beings, animals and environment. In additions, technical reviews are carried out from time to time to assess the safety of pesticides for their continued use. Based on which, the Government, inter alia, has banned 40 pesticides in the country.<br/>****<br/>

records.qtitle: Disabled friendly infrastructure in public spaces
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a)	the steps taken by Government to build disabled-friendly zones, such as ramps and parking areas, in public spaces;<br/><br/>(b)	whether Government proposes to increase the number of public toilets which are disabled-friendly; and <br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT<br/><br/>(SHRI KRISHANPAL GURJAR)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c): Under the Scheme for implementation of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (SIPDA), funds are provided to States/UTs for creation of barrier free environment, namely, construction of lifts, ramps, accessible parking, accessible toilets, tactile flooring etc. for the benefit of persons with disabilities.  To successfully operationalize and create accessible environment, Government has launched a multisectoral “Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan)” as a nation-wide flagship campaign for achieving universal accessibility for PwDs. The Campaign also focus on enhancing the accessibility of government and public buildings. <br/><br/>              Under Swachh Bharat Mission(SBM), provisions have been made to ensure separate toilet and bathing facilities for disabled persons with ramp provision and braille signage. As per the Swachh Bharat Mission guidelines, all Community Toilets (CT) and Public Toilets (PT) must have disabled friendly toilets, irrespective of whether any disabled people reside/live in the vicinity of the toilets or not.<br/><br/>****<br/><br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a)	the estimates of slum population across the country, State-wise;<br/><br/>(b)	the steps taken by Government to collect surveys pertaining to slums between successive censuses;<br/><br/>(c)	the number of low-cost housing complexes constructed by Government during the last four years and the current year; and<br/><br/>(d)	the number of such houses that continue to remain vacant?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE <br/>MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS<br/><br/>      (SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI)<br/><br/>(a): As per the Population Census of India 2011, the estimated slum population across the country is 6,54,94,604. State/Union Territory (UT)-wise details of slum population are at Annexure-I. <br/><br/>(b): The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) does not conduct any specific survey pertaining to slums between successive censuses.  However, the MoHUA through its programmatic intervention viz. Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) {PMAY(U)} Mission has been making overarching efforts in providing housing with basic civic amenities to the urban poor including slum dwellers of towns/cities of the country by assisting States/UTs both technically and financially. <br/><br/>(c) & (d): The number of houses sanctioned, grounded, completed and unoccupied during the last four years and the current year under various housing schemes of the MoHUA is respectively 72,80,851, 38,67,191, 14,75,879 and 3,14,765.  <br/><br/>                *****<br/>

records.qtitle: Regulation of long working hours of CRPF Personnel
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: <br/>(a) the steps taken by Government to regulate and monitor the long working hours of CRPF Personnel;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government is aware that accommodation provided to the paramilitary forces is often unhygienic, not secure and ill-maintained; and<br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to monitor the accommodation provided to the personnel?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a): 	  Generally the working hours in the Central Reserve Police Forces are 8 hourly shifts. This, however, varies depending on operational exigencies. Necessary leave/ training reserve is built in the structure of Battalions so that the personnel get rest and leave. Measures have been taken to implement a transparent, rational and fair leave policy and to regulate duty hours to ensure adequate rest and leave.<br/>(b) & (c): 	 The forces have intimated that regular cleanliness is carried out at accommodations  and surrounding  area.  Senior   Officers  including   <br/><br/><br/>--2--  <br/>R.S.US.Q NO. 341 FOR 06.02.2019<br/>Medical Officers visit the accommodation provided to the force personnel and they always inspect its maintenance, the hygienic condition and security arrangements. The forces also monitor the accommodation/establishments under their command. Wherever infrastructure is provided by the State due to deployment of forces, forces use their own resources for continuous improvement of available infrastructure.<br/>************<br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has taken any steps to minimize air crashes, if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government checks safety requirements before providing flight permits, if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) whether Government takes strict and timely action on operators who deviate from the established safety norms, if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: The Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Jayant Sinha)<br/><br/>(a) Yes, Sir. DGCA has taken the following steps to minimise air crashes:<br/><br/>(i) As per the annual surveillance program, audit of the operators is carried out. Findings of audit report are followed up with the operator for compliance. The compliance of the action taken by the operator is further verified during the next audit.<br/><br/>(ii) Safety recommendations emanating from the investigation reports are followed up for implementation with the concerned agencies so as to prevent recurrence of similar incident in future. <br/><br/>(iii) Accident/incident data is regularly analyzed and based on the analysis<br/> Air Safety Circulars are issued to bring important observations/findings to the notice of the operators to avoid the recurrence of the accidents/incidents.<br/>(b) The Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) Section 3 Series C Part II, Part III and Part IV specify the minimum requirements for issue of permit to operate Air Transport Services  for schedule passenger, non- scheduled and cargo operations respectively.   The safety requirements are checked before issuance of flight permit to operators as per the procedure laid down in:<br/>1. Civil Aviation Publication (CAP) 3100- Air operation certification manual for scheduled operator<br/>2. Civil Aviation Publication (CAP) 3300- Air operation certification manual for scheduled commuter and non-scheduled operators.<br/>3. Civil Aviation Publication (CAP) 3400- Air operation certification manual for helicopter operations.<br/><br/>(c) DGCA takes strict and timely action on operators who deviate from the established safety norms. DGCA took 03 and 05 enforcement actions during the year 2017 and 2018 respectively against the operators.<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Regulatory mechanism for charter flights and helicopters
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: (a) the number of accidents resulting from charter flights and helicopters during the last four years and the current year;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government has put in place a regulatory mechanism for the operation of such charter flights and helicopters; and<br/><br/>(c) if so, the details thereof, and if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: The Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Jayant Sinha)<br/><br/>(a) Year wise detail of charter flight and helicopter accidents:<br/><br/>Year	 No. of accidents of Charter <br/><br/>             Flights and Helicopters<br/>2015               4<br/>2016               3<br/>2017               3<br/>2018               3<br/>2019              NIL<br/><br/>(b) & (c) The Scheduled and Non Scheduled Operator Permit Holders are permitted to undertake Charter operations and in case of Scheduled Operator, the same is permitted, provided their Schedule is not affected. The Air Operator Permit/Certificate is issued after the grant  of initial NOC and the applicant undergoing  successfully the Five Phase certification process as per applicable Air Operator Certification Manual i.e. CAP 3100/3300/3400. <br/>The Non Scheduled Operator Permit holders are allowed to operate Charter Flights as per Para 2.4 and 2.5  of CAR Section 3 Series C Part 3 as reproduced below-<br/>"2.4 The carriage of passengers by a non-scheduled operator''s permit holder may be performed on per seat basis or by way of chartering the whole aircraft on per flight basis, or both. There is no bar on the same aircraft being used for either purpose as per the requirement of customers from time to time. The operator is also free to operate a series of flights on any sector within India by selling individual seats but will not be permitted to publish time table for such flights. Operation of revenue charters to points outside India may also be undertaken as per paragraph 9.2.<br/><br/>2.5 A Non-Scheduled Operator is also allowed to operate revenue charter flights for a company within its group companies, subsidiary companies, sister concern, associated companies, own employees, including Chairman and members of the Board of Directors of the company and their family members, provided it is operated for remuneration, whether such service consists of a single flight or series of flights over any period of time."<br/><br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) the steps taken by Government to generate awareness about HIV in the country; <br/><br/>(b) the steps taken by Government to ensure that patients suffering from HIV are not discriminated against in society; and <br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to track the patients through HIV diagnosis to care and treatment?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL)<br/>(a):     The Government implements 360 degree multimedia campaigns along with mass media supported by outdoor media such as hoardings, bus panels, information kiosks, folk performances and exhibition vans to create awareness on HIV/AIDS and promoting services/facilities across the country. At the inter-personal level, training and sensitization programmes for Self-Help Groups, Anganwadi workers, ASHA, members of Panchayati Raj Institutions and other key stakeholders are also being organised to spread awareness about treatment and other facilities. In addition, awareness activities are conducted amongst High Risk Groups including Female Sex Workers, Men having Sex with Men, Injecting Drug Users, Hijra/ Transgenders and Bridge Population like  truck drivers, migrants etc. as part of Targeted Intervention projects.<br/>(b):     The Government of India has enacted the HIV & AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017.  The Act addresses discrimination against People Living with HIV (PLHIV) at workplace, education setting, health setting and public places.<br/> <br/>The act also provides a robust grievance redressal mechanism where compliant against discrimination would be disposed by Ombudsman at the state level.<br/><br/>(c):     The steps taken by Government to track the patients through HIV diagnosis to care and treatment include adoption of Test and Treat policy under which all patients diagnosed with HIV are put on Anti Retro Viral Treatment irrespective of their CD4 Count; Launch of Mission Sampark to reach out to all the lost to follow patients living with HIV and linking them back as much as possible to Anti Retro Viral Treatment. In addition, there is software to maintain the details of the patients to enable them on regular treatment. Also, counsellors ensure tracking of HIV positive patients through telephone and home visits in the case of  those who drop out between diagnosis and treatment to maintain their adherence to treatment.<br/>……………<br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) whether Government is taking any steps to sensitise people towards mental illness, if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(b) the number of Government-run mental heath facilities and hospitals established in the country in the last three years and the current year; and <br/><br/>(c) the details of the steps taken by Government to monitor the functioning of these hospitals?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL)<br/>(a):    To address the burden of mental disorders, the Government of India is implementing the National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) since 1982. Under this Programme, the Government is supporting implementation of the District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) in 517 districts of the country for detection, management and treatment of mental disorders/ illness. At the district level, funds are provided to each district under the DMHP for sensitization training of Community Health Workers and elected representatives of community at District Hospital/ Community Health Centre for awareness generation regarding early signs and community health seeking behavior for mental illness. Further, the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 provides that the appropriate Government shall take all measures to ensure that the Government Officials including police officers and other officers of the Government are given periodic sensitization and awareness training.<br/>(b) & (c):   Health being a State subject, it is the responsibility of the respective State Government to establish health facilities and hospitals in the State. However, as per available information there are 40 State run mental health Institutions in the country. Besides, three Central Mental Health Institutions viz. National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences, Bangalore, Lokopriya Gopinath Bordoloi Regional Institute of Mental Health, Tezpur and Central Institute of Psychiatry, Ranchi have been strengthened for augmenting the human resources in the areas of mental health and to provide quality mental health services in the country. <br/>Contd……<br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/>Further, with a view to increase the number of qualified mental health professionals in the country, the Government, under the NMHP, is implementing manpower development schemes for establishment of Centres of Excellence and strengthening/ establishment of Post Graduate (PG) Departments in mental health specialties. Till date, financial support has been provided for establishment of 25 Centres of Excellence and strengthening/ establishment of 47 Post Graduate (PG) Departments in mental health specialties in the country. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare regularly reviews and monitors the functioning of the three Central Mental Health Institutions and the Institutions supported under manpower development schemes of NMHP.<br/><br/>

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of AYURVEDA, YOGA & NATUROPATHY, UNANI, SIDDHA AND HOMOEOPATHY be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) the details of the medicinal plants available in the country; and <br/><br/>(b) the details of the steps being taken by Government for the farming, conservation, processing and promotion of such medicinal plants?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYURVEDA,<br/>YOGA & NATUROPATHY, UNANI, SIDDHA AND HOMOEOPATHY<br/>(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK)<br/>(a): As per information of the Botanical Survey of India (BSI), an organization under Ministry of Environment, Forests & Climate Change, Government of India, estimated more than 8,000 species of medicinal plants are found in India.<br/><br/>(b): The National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), Ministry of AYUSH is presently implementing following schemes to encourage farming / cultivation, conservation, processing and promotion of medicinal plants throughout the country:<br/>1.	Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National AYUSH Mission (NAM).  Under ‘Medicinal Plants’ component of the NAM scheme the large scale farming / cultivation of medicinal plants is being supported.  As per the scheme guidelines, the support is provided for:<br/><br/>(i)	Cultivation of prioritized medicinal plants on farmer’s land.<br/>(ii)	Establishment of nurseries for supply of quality planting material.<br/>(iii)	Post-harvest management.<br/>(iv)	Primary processing, marketing infrastructure etc.<br/>For cultivation, the support is provided as subsidy to farmers @ 30%, 50% and 75% based on cost of cultivation.<br/><br/>Contd………<br/>2.	Central Sector Scheme on “Conservation, Development and Sustainable Management of Medicinal Plants”.  Under the scheme, the project based support is provided for following activities:<br/>(i)	In-situ conservation through development of Medicinal Plants Conservation and Development Areas (MPCDAs).<br/>(ii)	In-situ/Ex-situ resource augmentation.<br/>(iii)	Ex-situ conservation through establishment of herbal gardens.<br/>(iv)	Livelihood linkages with Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs) / Panchayats / Van Panchayats / Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) / Self Help Groups (SHGs).<br/>(v)	IEC activities like Training / workshops / Seminars/ Conferences etc.<br/>(vi)	Research & Development.<br/>(vii)	Promotion of marketing and trade of medicinal plants produce.<br/><br/>3.	Voluntary Certification Scheme for Medicinal Plants Produce (VCSMPP). The scheme is aimed to encourage Good Agricultural Practices (GAPs) and Good Field Collection Practices (GFCPs) in medicinal plants and enhance quality and safety of their produce.<br/><br/>……………….<br/><br/>
