records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to compulsorily retire officials against whom cases of corruption by CBI are registered under FR 56 (j);

(b) if so, whether Government have identified the revenue officials having doubtful integrity;

(c) if so, the number of cases registered against revenue officials by CBI in each of the last three years togetherwith the details thereof; and

(d) the measures taken by Government to get these cases expedited?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN)

(a) to (d): Fundamental Rule (FR) 56(j) confers on the Government the right to retire a Government servant in public interest after he has attained a prescribed age, i.e., 50/55 years. The provisions of this Rule are invoked by the Government to weed out, from Government service, employees who have outlived their utility and have become ineffective as well as those whose integrity is doubtful.
However, the provisions of FR 56(j) are not applicable to Government employees against whom cases have been registered by the CBI. The registration of cases by CBI and action under FR 56 (j) have no direct relation. Thirty six cases have been registered by the CBI in respect of income tax officials during the years 1999, 2000 and 2001. The number of cases registered in respect of Customs & Central Excise officials during the years 1999, 2000, 2001 (upto May), is 29, 19 & 7 respectively. The progress of such cases registered by the CBI is monitored by the Central Vigilance Commission.

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) the reasons for lack of international level sports persons in the country ;

(b) whether the country also lacks sports infrastructure of international standards ; and

(c) if so, by when Government propose to provide the required infrastructure facilities of international level in the country ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS

(SUSHREE UMA BHARTI)

(a) to ( c): A statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO ( c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 280 FOR 7.12.2001 REGARDING SPORTS INFRASTRUCTURE .

(a) Severe financial constraints and the enormity of the challenge of sports promotion and development of sports infrastructure across the country are main reasons for the slow development of sports performance in the country. In addition, the ratio of persons participating in competitive sports is low in comparison with those participating in recreational sports - leading to lesser competition and consequently lower performance. Food habits, age of entry into a sports discipline , environment and motivation play a crucial role in deciding the level of performance of a sports person. Besides, sports is yet to be made an integral part of our educational curriculum. All factors mentioned above have affected the level of performance of sports persons in the country.

(b) No , Sir.

(c) On receipt of viable proposals , financial assistance is provided under schemes for creation of infrastructure facilities.

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to start some schemes for employment and income generation for the sex workers, in order to encourage them to reintegrate into the society;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the fresh steps taken by Government to eradicate child prostitution and their rehabilitation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SUMITRA MAHAJAN)

(a)&(b) Yes, Sir. The scheme proposes measures for social and economic rehabilitation of women in difficult circumstances including trafficked women or girls rescued from brothels or run away from other places.

(c) Advisory Committees on Child Prostitution have been set up at Central and State levels to address the issues in cooperation with NGO representatives. An amendment to the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 is underway for making punishment for traffickers more stringent. A network of Short Stay Homes has also been set up for protection and rehabilitation of the victims of prostitution.

(a): Yes, Sir, except during adverse weather conditions and during ban period ordered by various State Governments.

(b) & (c): Fishing community in coastal areas dry the fish normally by sun drying. In some centres sun drying is done hygienically, whereas, in some places improved handling and processing techniques are yet to be adopted.

(d) & (e): Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (CIFT) have developed some low cost technologies like: hygienic sun drying of fish spread on raised platform. This CIFT technology has been circulated among the Coastal States, Apex Fishery Cooperative Bodies and Fishery Colleges and Institutions.

(f) to (h): The Ministry has an ongoing scheme for funding R&D projects for development of such technology. Various institutions including Veterinary colleges, Agricultural Universities & Cooperatives are eligible to avail this assistance.

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have prepared a plan to increase generation of nuclear power in the next twenty years;

(b) if so, whether any details have been worked out with regard to setting up more nuclear power plants; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE

(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The present nuclear power capacity in the country is 2720 & MWe. It is proposed to be increased to about 20,000 MWe by

(c) the year 2020, subject to the availability of budgetary support from the Government. During the X Five Year Plan, nuclear power capacity of 1300 MWe is planned to be added by completion of TAPP 3&4-2x500 MWe (being uprated to 540 MWe) and Kaiga 3 (one 220 MWe, out of 2x220 MWe of Kaiga 3&4 units under construction) units. Thus, the total nuclear power capacity will reach 4020 MWe by the end of the X Plan. The proposals in the X Plan envisage the commencement of new schemes, to yield benefits for reaching a total nuclear

power capacity of 9935 MWe by end of XI Plan. Additional projects are also planned to be taken up in the XI Plan and beyond, to achieve a nuclear power capacity of about 20,000 MWe by the year 2020.
The above programme will however be subject to allocation of required plan outlays and Budgetary Support from the Government of India.

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there is an immediate need to increase lending in areas like agro-processing, bio-technology and horticulture by commercial banks with regular monitoring;

(b) whether loans are needed to be given in the education sector so that promising students are not deprived of education because of lack of funds; and

(c) if so, the steps Government are taking to relax loan norms for these activities?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL)

(a): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reported that traditional/non-traditional plantations and horticulture as also medium and long term loans to all plantations/ horticulture have already been included in Priority Sector and have been classified as Direct Finance to Agriculture. Loans given by banks to food & agro-processing sector are also included tinder priority sector lending and achievements are being monitored regularly by RBI.

(b} & fc): RBI has reported that a new educational loan scheme prepared by the Indian Banks Association (IBA) duly approved by the Government has been circulated among all scheduled commercial banks for implementation during this academic session itself. The salient features of the scheme are: > Cover courses in schools and colleges in India and abroad; > Loans up to Rs.7.5 lakhs for studies in India and up to Rs.15 lakhs for studies abroad; > No collateral or margin required for loans up to Rs.4 lakhs; > Interest on loans up to Rs.4 lakh will not exceed PLR and those above Rs.4 lakhs will be FLR + 1 percent; > Repayable over a period of 5 - 7 years after completion of the course. The New Education Loan Scheme has been introduced by all the public sector banks. records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF COAL AND MINES

(SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN)


(a) to (c):- A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN THE REPLIES TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.144 ASKED BY SHRI P.N.SIVA, FOR ANSWER ON 28.11.2001

(a) & (b): For the power plants recommended by Ministry of Power for long term coal linkage, Standing Linkage Committee

(Long Term) functioning in the Department of Coal, based on projected availability of coal & logistics furnished by coal companies and Railways, grants long term linkage to power plants.
Linkage order is issued by the Department of Coal with the following general conditions:-

i) A sum equivalent to the cost of one month’s value of coal supplies shall be deposited with the coal company concerned as earnest money on signing of the Fuel Supply Agreement.
ii) A further sum equivalent to two months’ value of coal supplies as commitment advance shall be deposited within one year of signing of the Fuel Supply Agreement.
iii) The developer shall enter into a Fuel Supply contract with the coal company within a year from the date of issue of linkage order. Linkage will automatically be cancelled, if this stipulation is not adhered to.

(c): The amount of one month’s deposit is not an advance but is an earnest money payable by the developer of the power plants on execution of Fuel Supply Agreement. This earnest money is refundable as per policy.

4TH POSITION
RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 144 (4TH POSITION FOR 28.11.2001) - NOTE FOR SUPPLEMENTARIES <><><>
INTRODUCTION
Long term linkages to power plants are decided by the Standing Linkage Committee (Long Term) for power functioning in the Department of Coal.
This Committee is chaired by Additional Secretary, Department of Coal, having members from Planning Commission, Ministry of Power, Ministry of Railways, Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Surface Transport, apart from Chairman, Coal India Limited, CMDs, of coal producing subsidiaries of Coal India Limited, CMD, CMPDIL, CMD, Singareni Collieries Company Limited, and Chairman, NTPC.
Long term linkage to power plants is decided by the Standing Linkage Committee (Long Term) keeping in view the recommendation of the Ministry of Power and the projected availability of coal and logistics furnished by coal company and Ministry of Railways. The linkage is subject to the following general conditions.

i) A sum equivalent to the cost of one month’s value of coal supplies shall be deposited with the coal company concerned on signing of the Fuel Supply Agreement.

ii) A further sum equivalent to two months’ value of coal supplies shall be deposited within one year of signing of the Fuel Supply Agreement.

iii) The developer shall enter into a Fuel Supply contract with the coal company within a year from the date of issue of linkage order. Linkage will automatically be cancelled, if this stipulation is not adhered to.
The decision of charging one month`s coal value as earnest money deposit (EMD) and another two months` coal value as commitment advance (CA) from the developer of the power plant was taken in an inter ministerial meeting convened by Secretary

(Coal) on 15th May, 1996 and its minutes were circulated vide letter No.23022/3/93-CPD-Vol.III dated 22nd May, 1996.
The Coal Supply Agreements for the new Power Plants are long term agreements with firm commitments of quantity, quality, timely supply, payments, related bonus and penalties as well as determination of quality & quantity. It also includes the provisions of Earnest Money Deposit as well as Commitment Advance and related clauses dealing with the aspects of forfeiture, interest, refund/adjustments of these deposits. These are legally enforceable commercial agreements.
The Coal Supply Agreements against the linkages granted after May 1996 for SEBs and NTPC are yet to be executed. The EMD becomes due only at the time of execution of the agreement.
As regards the Independent Power Producers (IPP), each of the agreements (executed, initialed or those which are under negotiations) have the provision relating to EMD & CA.

Demand & Supply of coal to the power sector

(a) Power Sector is the bulk consumer of coal. This Sector is accorded highest priority in terms of despatches and movement of coal.

(b) Nearly 70% of the coal produced in the country is consumed by the power sector.

(c) It may be noted that the despatches to power sector have been consistently increasing over the years (except 1998- 99). Both CIL & SCCL have been able to meet the growing demand of that sector in full.

(d) The details of demand (as assessed by the Planning Commission) and despatches of coal to power sector from 1997-98 onwards are given in the following table:

Joint Sampling/Third Party Sampling
In order to ensure that disputes on grade, quality/quantity on supplies of coal to power stations are minimised, the Ministries of Coal and Power, in consultation with the Council of Power Utilities and Coal India Limited have introduced a policy of joint sampling and third party sampling. Wherever the coal companies and Power Utilities mutually agree, joint sampling can be resorted to at loading and unloading ends. In other cases, an independent third party can be engaged. This alternative system permits an independent third party/agency for sampling of coal to be taken at the loading and unloading end by the same independent third party, which is appointed with mutual consultation.
The system of third party sampling/analysis has been introduced since April 1999 progressively in a number of Power Houses. This has shown positive results and the disputes have gone down considerably. Provisions are also incorporated for analysis of referee samples through mutually accepted Government/Public sector laboratories where wide variance (more than 5% UHV) are noticed in the results of two sides. Therefore, the possibility of disputes on account of quality/grade has been substantially minimized.

Qn (a). What is the system of short-term linkages and coal allotments to power sector ?
Ans. In order to ensure regular supply of coal to thermal power stations, standing linkage committee- short term is functioning under the aegis of Ministry of Coal with Addl. Secretary, MoC as chairman of the committee. The other members of the committee are from Ministries of Railways, Power, Central Electricity Authority and coal producing companies. Based on the projection of long term linkage, power generation target of power houses, requirement of coal by individual power station as indicated by CEA, available coal stock with the power stations, availability of coal at various supplying sources and available transport logistics, the Standing Linkage Committee (Short Term) allocates source and modes wise monthly coal linkage of power stations on quarterly basis. Thus, while long term linkage is a perspective plan to identify source for requisite quantity of coal for a power station along with mode of transport, the short term linkage translates the perspective plan into a quarterly action plan on the basis of the prevailing ground situation at the time of allocating coal to a power plant.
Qn. (b). What is the rationale for charging EMD?
Ans. From the time linkage is given by the Standing Linkage Committee (Long Term), CIL gets virtually committed to the supply of coal and, therefore, CIL has to take a number of actions including advance actions for implementation of the project which cost substantial money. In such an event, if IPP backs out for any reason whatsoever, certain expenditure may turn out to be infructuous. This is more so in those cases where the power plant is being set up at pithead and the mine developed by Coal India becomes virtually captive to the power plant.
Qn (c). Are there any FSAs, which have been signed by coal companies and whether they contain any provision for one month’s earnest money deposit?
Ans. Coal companies had finalised a model draft agreement with Council of Power Utility/CEA based on which the FSAs (short term) were to be executed by all SEBs. However, only some of the SEBs have executed the short term FSA with coal companies . These are PSEB, HSEB, RSEB, MSEB, KPCL etc. Coal companies have also negotiated and executed agreement with NTPC in August, 1999 covering coal supply to all the existing pit head power plants of NTPC. In all these agreements, there was no provision of depositing one month’s coal sale value as earnest money, as these are old power stations getting supplies from existing mines.

Qn. (j) What is the amount of total outstanding dues to CIL from all sectors?

Ans. The total outstanding dues to CIL from all sectors as on 31.10.2001 areRs.6665.10 crores. Out of this, Rs.2392.75 crores are disputed, while Rs.4272.35 crores are undisputed dues. The total dues recoverable from power sector are Rs.5947.53 crores (about 90% of the total dues). The disputed amount from power sector was Rs.1891.02 crores, while the balance amount of Rs.4056.51 crores is undisputed. Details of SEB-wise and company- wise dues are given in Annexure IV & V.

Qn. (k) What steps have been taken for recovery of the outstanding dues?
Ans. The following steps have been taken by the Government / Coal India Limited to recover the outstanding dues from the State Electricity Boards:
i. Coal India Limited (CIL) has been advised to supply coal to power utilities only against advance payment or letter of credit. (Cash and Carry)
ii. Coal India Limited and it subsidiary coal companies have been persistently following up with the consumers in diverse sectors for settlement of dues.
iii. Recovery of dues by way of adjustment against power bills is also being done in respect of certain power utilities.
iv. Umpires have been appointed for resolving the disputed dues between the coal companies and SEBs.
v. Deductions from Central Plan assistance-Government has also decided to deduct the outstanding dues of Coal India limited as on 31.12.1996 through the mechanism of cuts from the Central Plan Assistance to the State Governments, subject to certain ceilings. The total recovery so far has been Rs.858.40. crores.
vi. Government is considering to put in place, a securitization scheme for recovery of dues.
Qn. (l) What is securitization of outstanding dues?
Ans. Attempts are being made by the Government for the last 2-3 years to evolve a guarantee scheme / securitization scheme to cover the outstanding dues from SEBs to the Central PSUs in the coal, power and other sectors. Government constituted an expert Group under the chairmanship of Dr.M.S. ahluwalia, the then Member, Planning commission in March, 2001 to recommend measures for one-time settlement of outstanding dues. TheGroup submitted its report in May, 2001. the broad recommendations of the Expert Group are as follows:
i. A scheme was recommended for securitization the outstanding dues and converting them into state government bonds with a partial waiver. According to this scheme, outstanding dues for coal till 28.02.2001 were to be eligible for the purpose of one-time settlement and may be converted into bonds to be issued by the respective governments. The principal dues are to be paid in full and interest /surcharge to be waived by 50%.
ii. The bonds will be purchased by the PSUs (coal companies) and the proceeds will be adjusted in their books of accounts against the outstanding dues of SEBs. The bonds will be tax free and interest rate of 8.5% per annum to be payable every six months.
iii. to facilitate marketability and servicing of these bonds, the total amount to be settled may be divided into 20 equal parts and bonds for every part may be issued as a separate tranche. The first tranche may be redeemable after 5 years and each subsequent tranche may be redeemed after every six months thereafter, till all the 20 tranches are redeemed in a period of 15 years.
iv. Compliance of the Scheme would enable the State Government to receive an annual cash incentive equal to 4% of the nominal value of the bonds for 4 years commencing from 1.4.2001.
v. As a pre-requisite for one time settlement of outstanding dues, the respective State Governments must enter into binding commitments that would ensure timely payment of current dues by the respective SEBs. SEBs should make payment of current dues within 60 days of billing or 45 days of receipt of bill, whichever is later.
The report of the Expert Group has since been considered by a High Level Empowered Group (HLEG) comprising the Deputy Chairman, Planning Commission, Union Finance Minister, Union Minister of Power and nine Chief Ministers. The HLEG has unanimously accepted the recommendations of the Expert Group with the two modifications as under:
a. 60% waiver of surcharge instead of 50% proposed by the Expert Group. b. the incentives for achieving reform based milestones to be increased to 6% in the first year and 5 % in the second year as against 4 recommended by the Group.
The total admitted principal coal sale dues as on 28.2.2001

(position as on 31.8.2001), which are to be considered for securitization are Rs.2408.84 crores and the total disputed dues are Rs.1507.45 crores. Further, the total dues on account of interest @ 12% on admitted principal dues is Rs.1398.32 crores of which Rs.1305.18 crores have not been acknowledged by SEBs as dues for payment. The interest on disputed principal dues in Rs.743.96 crores. The dues owed to Eastern Coalfields Limited by entities under West Bengal Government are in the process of adjustment against dues of cess owed to West Bengal Government. Further, Mahanadi Coalfields Limited is not opting for securitization, as it would prefer to settle the dues directly with the SEBs. Excluding the admitted principal dues of ECL and MCL, the net admitted principal dues comes to Rs.1330.62 crores. Of the interest on admitted principal dues for CIL subsidiaries other than ECL and MCL, only an amount of Rs.71.03 crores in respect of SECL have been accepted by the SEBs (GEB and MPEB). The net amount after 60% waiver of undisputed interest of Rs.71.03 crores comes to Rs.28.41 crores. Therefore, for the present only an amount of Rs.1359.03 crores (Rs.1330.62 + Rs.28.41 crores) is available for securitization.

The implementation of the recommendations of the Expert Group as accepted by the High Level Empowered Group requires the execution of a Tripartite Agreement between the Government of India, Reserve Bank of India and the State Governments. The draft Tripartite Agreement has already been circulated to the coal companies and Secretary (Coal) has written to Chief Secretaries of States receiving coal supplies for finalization of the Tripartite Agreement. Ministry of Power is preparing a Cabinet Paper after 50% of the States (9 states) agree. Andhra Pradesh has already agreed and Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are expected to sign the agreements soon. If the 9 States agree, the Bond may be issued by March 2002.

records.qtitle: PURCHASING POWER BY MAJOR CONSUMERS FROM POWER GENERATION UNITS .
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have taken a decision to allow major power consuming institutions to purchase power directly from power generation units;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the definition of major power consumers;

(c) whether Government have decided to levy a surcharge on these consumers; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor and whether the decision will lead to increase in the power tariff due to which the very purpose of the decision will be defeated?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )

(a) to (d) : As per provisions of Section 43A(c) of Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948, a generating company can sell power to any person with the approval of the Government or Governments concerned.
The Electricity Bill 2001 as introduced in Lok Sabha in August 2001, empowers the State Electricity Regulatory Commission to allow open access in distribution in phases after cross subsidies are eliminated. It also provides that such open access may be allowed before cross subsidies are eliminated on payment of surcharge in addition to the charges for wheeling as may be determined by the State Commission. Such surcharge will be utilized to meet the requirement of current level of cross subsidy.

records.qtitle: CREATION OF A DEPARTMENT OF BORDER MANAGEMENT IN MHA .
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether a Department of Border Management has been set up within the Union Home Ministry;

(b) if so, the parameters, functions and other details of the Department; and

(c) if not, by when such a department is likely to be set up?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO )

(a),(b) & (c): The Group of Ministers has, inter alia, recommended that a separate Department of Border Management may be created under the overall charge of the Home Secretary. It should monitor, coordinate and oversee Border Management. A detailed proposal for the creation of a separate Department of Border Management is at present under consideration. Pending sanction of additional officers and staff for the proposed Department of Border Management, a Border Management Division has been created in the Ministry by giving additional charge to a senior officer and providing minimum skeletal staff through internal adjustment.

records.qtitle: EXPERT COMMITTEE ON INCREASING THE LIFE OF CURRENCY NOTES .
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether a committee of Experts was formed to examine the possibility of increasing the life of Indian currency notes ;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the action taken by the Government on the recommendation of the Committee ?
records.ans_text:
)
Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance(Shri Balasaheb Vikhe Patil)

( a) & (b). Yes, Sir. The Government had set up a Committee of Experts on 15th October,1999 to examine various proposals for increasing the life of Indian bank notes. General Manager Currency Note Press (CNP), Nashik was nominated as the Convenor of the said Committee alongwith six other members including General Manager, Bank Note Press (BNP), Dewas: Head of the Department, Security Paper Mill (SPM), Hoshangabad; Chief General Manager, Department of Currency Management (DCM), Reserve Bank of India; two representatives from Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Ltd (BRBNML), RBI and Financial Adviser, India Security Press(ISP), Nashik. The Committee submitted its report during August, 2001.

( c ) The recommendations of the Committee are under consideration in the Department of Economic Affairs.

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the news item captioned, `FIs; promoters busy restructuring steel loans to avoid NPAs` appearing in the Indian Express dated the 20th August, 2001;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the steps taken by Government to recover the loan from the private steel companies due to which NPAs have accumulated?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(a) to (c) Government has seen the news item captioned `FIs Promoters busy restructuring steel loans to avoid NPAs` appeared in the Indian Express dated 20th August, 2001. Steel industry is going through a difficult phase for various reasons such as non-materialisation of the projected demand, the glut in the international market and depreciation in the value of certain currencies. While the domestic steel prices slumped, various input costs continued to escalate. The problems were compounded by subdued capital market conditions due to which the companies were not able to mobilize the envisaged funds by way of equity and achieve financial closure. It was in this backdrop, the restructuring package has been considered for the large size steel projects by the Financial Institutions. However in accordance with the practices and usages customary amongst the banks and in conformity with provisions of statutes governing the financial institutions as also the provisions of the Public Financial Institutions

(Obligations as to Fidelity and Secrecy) Act, 1983, the information in respect of the constituents of the Public Financial Institutions cannot be divulged.

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL)

(a) & (b): No Sir, At present there is no proposal under consideration of Government to merge nationalised banks.

(c) : The Narsimham Committee had recommended in its report that initiatives for mergers between public sector banks should emanate from the management of the concerned banks and should be based on synergy and business complementarity

(d),(e)&(f): No nationalised bank has so far made any application for merger with another bank.

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether extra deep brown steel is being imported for the automobile sector in the country;

(b) if so, the details in this regard and the amount incurred/being incurred;

(c) whether SAIL or other steel manufacturing units are not producing extra deep brown steel; and

(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR STEEL (SHRI BRAJA KISHORE TRIPATHY)

(a)&(b): Extra Deep Drawing (EDD) grade steel, which is made from Hot Rolled/Cold Rolled Coils/ Sheets, is used in the Automobile Sector. Around fifty percent of the CR Coils/Sheets imported into the country is of EDD quality and is consumed by the Automobile Sector as well as the White-Goods Sector. In the last year (2000-01), 246 thousand tonnes of CR Sheets/Coils, worth Rs. 493 crore, were imported by India.

(c)&(d): Many producers, including SAIL, are making Deep Drawing and Extra Deep Drawing quality of steel in India. However, the products of only a few match the international quality, required by the automobile sector.

(b) whether any complaints have been received against phosphatic fertilizer producers for the poor quality of the products and bogus claims for subsidy;

(c) if so, the details thereof and the action taken against the defaulters; and

(d) the procedure adopted to verify the claims for subsidy?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS

(SHRI S B MOOKHERJEE)

(a): The year-wise amount of subsidy disbursed under the Concession Scheme for de-controlled phosphatic and potassic fertilisers during the last three years is as under:- 
Year			Amount of Subsidy in Rs. Crore
1998-99			3789.94
1999-2000		4500
2000-01			4319


(b) & (c):	The Government over the years has been taking action based on  
individual  complaints and  newspaper reports which generally relate to fraudulent claims of subsidy and other malpractices under the Concession Scheme for de-controlled phosphatic and potassic fertilisers as also regarding  supply of poor quality of fertilisers mainly relating to Single Super Phosphate (SSP).  The concerned State Governments are then requested to investigate into the 
allegations for taking  appropriate action  under the provisions of Fertiliser Control Order (FCO).  Pending receipt of recommendations/findings of the State 
Governments, further release of subsidy to the concerned unit is withheld by the 
Central Government.  Thereafter, based on findings/ recommendations of the 
State Government, recovery of the subsidy amount claimed by the involved 
unit/company is effected by the Central Government.  The State Government of 
Punjab is presently carrying out investigations against some of its SSP units. The State Government of Bihar has also been requested to look into the allegations regarding impropriety in the matter of issue of certification of sales by the State authorities.  Processing of subsidy claims has been withheld in all such cases where completion of required investigation is pending.  The State Government of Uttar Pradesh had submitted the report in respect of the enquiry conducted against all its SSP units. The decision taken in concurrence with the UP Government on future course of action in the matter has been communicated to the State Government.


(d)	Under the Concession Scheme, the processing of concession claims is 
carried out in accordance with the procedure laid down thereunder, which, inter-
alia includes final settlement of subsidy claims after sales verification by the 
concerned State Government in prescribed proforma forming basis for final 
settlement of the claim. Further, in order to put a curb on sale of non standard 
SSP to farmers and need to promote use of specified grades of rock phosphate, 
under the new guidelines a Technical & Audit Inspection Cell (TAC) has been 
constituted to conduct first (1st) time as well as six-monthly inspections of SSP manufacturers for ensuring usage of specified grades of rock phosphate from 
sources notified by the Department of Fertilizers from time to time. Certain grades of rock phosphate along with sources have since been notified by the Department of Fertilizers.

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) the facilities presently available for the rehabilitation of the war disabled; and

(b) the number of disabled benefited from these schemes during the last three years, year-wise?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE (SHRI U.V. KRISHNAM RAJU) MINISTRY OF DEFENCE


(a) & (b): A statement is attached. STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) & (b) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4163 FOR 30.8.2001 REGARDING REHABILITATION OF WAR DISABLED. The war disabled who are fit for civil jobs in Central Government Departments, are eligible on priority-I for employment against Groups ‘C’ and ‘D’ posts, for which, recruitment is made through the Directorate General of Employment and Training. They can also avail of the benefit of loan assistance on liberalised terms under self- employment schemes to set up tiny/small scale industries, small scale service enterprises, undertake agriculture and allied activity, set up Khadi and village industries in rural areas. Besides, Queen Mary Technical Institute, Pune, a private charitable institution, conducts ITI recognised vocational trades training courses for disabled ex- Servicemen to facilitate their rehabilitation. In addition, paraplegic homes at Kirkee and Mohali are being run for rehabilitation of paraplegic and tetraplegic ex-Servicemen. Disabled soldiers are also provided artificial limbs by Artificial Limbs Centres.
Monetary Benefits:- The Armed Forces personnel disabled in war or war like operations are given war injury pension at the rate of reckonable emoluments last drawn if the degree of disablement is 100% and this is proportionately reduced if the disability is less than 100%. The disabled Officers/Junior Commissioned Officers/Other Ranks, invalidated out of service, are covered under the Army Group Insurance Scheme for insurance amount ranging from Rs. 80,000/- to Rs. 4 lakhs in the case of Officers and Rs. 37,500/- to Rs. 1,87,500/- in the case of Junior Commissioned Officers/Other Ranks, depending upon the level of disability.
The Armed Forces personnel boarded out of service due to injuries sustained in Kargil operation have been given ex- gratia grant from National Defence Fund, ranging from Rs.

3.0 lakhs to Rs. 6.0 lakhs, depending upon the level of injuries on completion of necessary procedural requirements. They have also been granted Rs. 5 lakhs from this fund for acquiring a dwelling unit or for making addition/alterations/renovation of the existing units.
Information about the number of war disabled who have been benefited from the various schemes is not centrally monitored.

records.qtitle: PROJECTS FOR UTILISATION OF SPECIAL CENTRAL ASISTANCE .
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have asked States to set up projects for utilisation of Special Central Assistance;

(b) if so, the guidelines for such Special Assistance Projects;

(c) whether any representations have been received from social activists for any such projects in Andhra Pradesh in the year 2000-2001 ; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT (SMT. MANEKA GANDHI)

(a) & (b) The States/UTs have been asked to prepare project proposals for utilization of Special Central Assistance (SCA) by dovetailing up to 50% of the unit cost limiting to Rs. 10,000 per beneficiary as subsidy out of SCA and balance amount as loan from National Scheduled Castes Finance & Development Corporation for assisting Scheduled Castes families, living below poverty line, in an integrated manner, as well as setting up required infrastructure for supporting the activities and provision of required forward and backward linkages.

(c) &(d) Dr. P. Puallarao, West Godavari District, had requested for assisting SC families belonging to the poorest section in the West Godawari District. The matter has been referred to the State Secretary, Deptt. of Social Welfare, for appropriate action, as per guidelines.

records.qtitle: STUDY ON HARAPPAN CIVILIZATION UNDER WATER .
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a team of scientists from National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), on one of its routine offshore surveys stumbled upon the ruins of Harappan Civilization under water ;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether any systematic study of the material discovered has been carried out;

(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and

(e) whether Government would set up any special team of scientists and indologists to carry out a full-fledged survey of the area and if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF OCEAN DEVELOPMENT

( DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI)

(a) & (b): National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai while carrying out multidisciplinary underwater surveys off Gujarat coast during October, 2000- March, 2001, located archaeological sites in the Gulf of Cambay at 30 to 40 m water depth extending over a length of 9 km, west of Hazira. During surveys NIOT came across a stretch of formations, typical of the riverine regime in the middle of the sea. The state of the art side scan surveys have picked up images that reveal excellent geometric objects which are normally man made. The area is seen to be lined with well laid house basement like features partially covered by sand waves and ripples.

(c) & (d): The study conducted was on the basis of the under water acoustic images. To confirm the age of these under water structures, samples have to be collected from the study area and taken for dating studies. Since the sea conditions were not conducive for carrying out such studies during the period of observation, it is now proposed to carry out sampling cruises at the site of the archaeological findings after October, 2001, subject to the weather conditions permitting.

(e): The proposed study would be conducted by a team of scientists drawn from National Institute of Ocean Technology, National Institute of Oceanography and other organizations which are involved in such activities. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) would also be associated with this study.

records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Reserve Bank of India has recently issued new guidelines for the Non-Banking Financial Companies;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor;

(c) whether these guidelines would govern the Residuary Non-Banking companies also; and

(d) if so, the details of the regulatory frame work which has been put in place to implement these guidelines?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL)

(a) & (b): The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has put in place a comprehensive regulatory and supervisory framework aimed at protecting the interests of depositors and ensuring that the NBFCs function on sound and healthy lines. Recently, RBI issued the Asset-Liability Management (ALM) Guidelines for Non- Banking Financial Companies as a part of the overall system for effective risk management in their various portfolios. As per the guidelines, NBFCs, which have asset size of Rs.100.00 crore and above or public deposits of Rs.20.00 crore and above as per their balance sheet as on 31.3.2001, should put in place an ALM system which is required to be implemented by the year ending 31.3.2002. The NBFCs have been advised that it would be desirable to constitute an Asset Liability Management Committee under the charge of Chief Executive Officer or other Senior Executive with specialist members for carrying out the spadework for formalising ALM system in the institution.

(c): The Asset Liability Management Guidelines are applicable to the Residuary Non-Banking Companies also which fulfil the conditions of asset size of Rs.100.00 crore and above or public deposits of Rs.20.00 crore and above as per their balance sheet as on 31.3.2001.


(d) : A new regulatory framework has been announced in January, 1998 to ensure that only well run NBFCs are allowed to access public deposits. The Reserve Bank of India has been taking various regulatory and supervisory measures to ensure a healthy growth of NBFC sector as also to provide safety to the depositors` money. For overseeing the implementation of the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 and the Directions and instructions issued by RBI thereunder, RBI has put in place a strong Regulatory Framework. This includes subjecting the NBFCs to the scrutiny of their applications to determine their eligibility as per the criteria enunciated in the RBI Act for issue of a Certificate of Registration, on-site inspections for ascertaining the level and quality of adherence by the entities inspected to the regulatory norms prescribed by RBI in relation to deposit taking activities, quality of assets, capital adequacy, etc., off-site surveillance and market intelligence system. The Statutory Auditors of NBFCs have also been assigned a particular role to report directly to the Bank the irregularities, if any, noticed by them in the working of an NBFC. Moreover, Chapter III-B, III-C and V of the RBI Act were amended in 1997, vesting considerable powers with the RBI for effective supervision over Non-Banking Financial Companies to ensure that they integrate their functioning with the Indian financial system.

records.qtitle: REVISION OF PAY SCALES OF STATION MASTERS
records.name: Tiruchi Siva
records.qn_text:

(c) whether Railway Board has come with a set of proposals to change the present mode of supply of uniforms, if so, what is the stand in granting the uniform allowance to Station Masters at par with railway nursing staff ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH)

(a) Pay scales allotted to Station Masters, Yard Masters and Shunting Masters arc as per the recommendations of the V Central Pay Commission as accepted by the Government Yard Masters and Shunting Masters form a separate cadre with distinctly different channel of career progression and they arc not subordinate to Station Masters.

(b) After the receipt of the Strike Notice, conciliation proceedings were hold by the Dy. Chief Labour Commissioner(C), New Delhi and the stand of the Ministry on the demands of the Association was explained to him. No positive assurance was given on any of the demands raised by the Association.

(c) The Uniform Committee, 1995 set up to review the entire aspect of supply of uniform to eligible railway employees have recommended supply of cloth and stitching charges to certain public image categories, which also includes the category of Station Master. These recommendations are presently under consideration.

records.subject: Need to Constitute a tribunal for the Mekedatu Balancing Reservoir cum Drinking Water Project.
records.SM_Text:
?Shri Tiruchi Siva:

I seek to raise the matter of urgent importance regarding the proposed dam at Mekedatu by Karnataka on Cauvery, an inter-state river, close to the borders of Tamil Nadu. This project is a unilateral initiative by the state of Karnataka which does not have the concurrence of the lower riparian state of Tamil Nadu in the basin. It goes against the constitutional mandate of division of subjects since the regulation of inter state rivers is a union subject. It also fringes upon the principle laid down by the honorable Supreme Court in 2007 which restricted upper riparian states to not take any action affecting the scheduled deliveries of water to the lower riparian states. There have been instances of non-compliance by Karnataka of the Supreme Court orders and the Tribunal award, CWMA and this project would further enable Karnataka to obstruct the flow of water as an upper riparian state. Cauvery is a deficit basin with apportioned water. It has no surplus for the proposed reservoir without compromising with the basic needs of Tamil Nadu which would drastically affect the farmers and their livelihood. Tamil Nadu State Assembly has unanimously passed the resolution against the said project. I hereby urge the government to not approve the DPR of the said project and constitute a tribunal with regards to Mekedatu dam to save the livelihood of farmers in Tamil Nadu.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for implementation of a National Road Safety Mission.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Tiruchi Siva: Road safety is a multifaceted challenge, spanning policing, public health, social behaviour, and urban planning and mobility. Adequate attention is required to be paid to these sectors. The Supreme Court has flagged that electronic enforcement standards need to be implemented, but little action has been taken in this regard. Ambulance availability and emergency preparedness vary widely, especially in rural areas. The lack of timely trauma care often leads to preventable deaths. Separate initiatives focusing on road safety currently exist, undertaken by central and local authorities. However, such patchwork legislation and fragmented strategy have yielded weak results. The number of road accidents and their severity have been steadily increasing. In 2024 alone, 1.77 lakh people have died in road accidents, which averages to about 485 persons a day. More than 4.6 lakh people have been injured in 2023. Over-speeding is responsible for 7 in 10 of these deaths.? India?s road accident fatality rate stands at 11.89 per 100,000 people. This poses a great economic burden of roughly 3% of the country?s GDP annually. Against this backdrop, human-centric interventions - which prioritize pedestrian safety and public transportation, and strengthen trauma care facilities ? are essential. Coordinated efforts across agencies, alongside strict enforcement of traffic laws, could save many lives. I urge the Government to establish and implement a National Road Safety Mission.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand of securing rights and protections for domestic workers.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Tiruchi Siva: The lack of comprehensive legal protections for domestic workers has long plagued India. Despite their vital role in households, they suffer from exploitation and unsafe working conditions. Domestic work in India is largely unregulated. Asper the National Domestic Workers? Movement (NDWM), 90% of India?s domestic workers are women or children aged 12to75, with 25% under age-14. Most are illiterate and engaged in tasks such as cooking and cleaning, traditionally seen as women?s work and considered subservient. Most of these workers lack formal contracts or protection under recently passed Labor Codes, leaving them vulnerable to exploitation. This situation is worsened by societal attitudes in their better-off employers, who regard domestic work as menial labor rather than a profession deserving dignity. The lack of proper implementation of existing legal protections allows employers to exploit workers without consequence. The Domestic Workers (Registration, Social Security, and Welfare) Bill, proposed by the National Commission of Women in 2009is yet to be implemented. To protect domestic workers, we must enact robust legislation ensuring fair wages, safe conditions, and social security. The recent direction from the Supreme Court, calling on the government to enact a separate law for domestic workers, only reinforces the urgency of these reforms. I demand that the Government should look into it.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for restoring education to State List for a more effective system.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Tiruchi Siva: This is to urge the Government to restore education in India to the State List to empower states to address local needs and uphold federalism. Historically a State List subject, it was shifted to the Concurrent List during the Emergency in 1976 as a centralizing measure. This decision, made under extraordinary circumstances, has since become redundant and increasingly misaligned with India?s diverse educational landscape. India?s vast diversity - with 26 Crore students and the vast gap in the literacy rate of Bihar compared with Kerala and Tamil Nadu - demonstrates the need for localized policymaking.

????????? Centrally-driven education policies overlook regional nuances, leading to inefficiencies. For instance, Eklavya Model Residential Schools, meant for tribal students, face challenges stemming from centralized hiring. Teachers recruited centrally struggle with regional languages, creating a disconnect that hampers learning. Tamil Nadu has consistently opposed NEET, since it restricts students from rural areas and those educated in the state board syllabus.

????????? States are better equipped to design policies tailored to their specific socio-cultural landscapes. Decentralization allows states to innovate, ensuring education systems are responsive to local needs. Returning education to the State List would restore states? autonomy, enhance accountability, and enable localized strategies crucial for improving educational outcomes in a diverse country like India.

I urge Government to look into it.

(Ends)

records.subject: Rampant Misuse of Quotas For Civil Services Examination
records.SM_Text:
Shri Tiruchi Siva: The rampant misuse of reservations intended for people with disabilities (PWD) and Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) for recruitment of civil servants is a grave issue that casts a shadow on the sanctity of our public service institutions. Various instances have recently come to light where candidates are falsely claiming disabilities or economic hardships to secure a competitive edge, undermining the principle of justice these provisions were designed to uphold. This alarming trend not only deprives genuinely deserving candidates of their rightful opportunities but also erodes public confidence in our well-intentioned reservation policies. It is a blatant exploitation of an essential system needed to uplift the marginalized, discriminated, and long-suppressed sections of society, thereby turning it into a tool for deceit. It is essential to implement rigorous verification processes and enforce stringent penalties for those found guilty of making false claims. Periodic audits and assessments should be conducted, including regular net-worth verifications, medical examinations for disability confirmation etc. Furthermore, robust legislative safeguards are required to close out any loopholes that enable such exploitation. I urge the government to act decisively and protect the integrity of our essential reservation policies. Strengthening verification processes, imposing stringent penalties for false claims, and introducing new legislation to close out loopholes will ensure that opportunities reach those who are genuinely deserving.

 

(Ends)

records.subject: Holistic Care for New Mothers: Addressing Postnatal Maternal Mental Health
records.SM_Text:
Shri Tiruchi Siva: Postnatal maternal mental healthcare is a critical issue that affects the well-being of countless Indian mothers. While we have made significant strides in maternal and child healthcare, mental health of new mothers remains overlooked. Postpartum depression (PPD) is a severe and prevalent condition, affecting 22% of mothers in India. It impacts the mother?s health, and has long-term implications for child-development and overall well-being of a family. Despite its prevalence, PPD often goes undiagnosed and untreated due to lack of awareness, social stigma, and inadequate mental healthcare infrastructure. A major component in addressing this issue is the role of Auxiliary Nurse Midwives. ANMs are often the first point of contact for new mothers in rural areas. Their success in maternal and child healthcare is commendable, but their training in mental health for identifying and managing PPD, requires significant enhancement. A study based in Pune demonstrated that targeted training programs can significantly improve ANMs ability to manage high-risk cases, including those involving mental-health concerns. Widespread training is essential to equip them with necessary skills to address PPD. We require legislation that mandates mental health screening and support as part of routine postnatal care. Comprehensive training modules should be developed for ANMs and other healthcare workers, focusing on maternal mental health. Nationwide awareness campaigns will help destigmatize postpartum depression, encouraging mothers to seek help by establishing community-based support groups. I urge the government to prioritize postnatal maternal mental healthcare and ensure that new mothers receive the holistic care they deserve, fostering healthier families.

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand of statehood for Puducherry
Regarding High Vacancies in Central Universities
records.SM_Text:
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (Tamil Nadu):? Sir, higher educational institutions significantly contribute to shaping young talent and the future of the country.? But for years many administrative and teaching positions have remained vacant in various Central universities.? This causes reduced student enrolment, issues on infrastructure development, research funding and student services, increased workload on existing faculty and restricted research output and innovation.?

????????? Over 6,500+ faculty positions are vacant across the country - Delhi University (900), Allahabad University (622), Banaras Hindu University (532) and Aligarh Muslim University (498) and JNU (326), Jamia Millia Islamia (223), Tripura University (146), Central University of Kashmir (116), Central University of Haryana (120), Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University (236) as per Ministry of Education, 2022.?

????????? The condition is dire especially for the University of Delhi, one of Indias premier institutions.? Delhi University and its colleges started selection for permanent positions after a gap of 10 years only last September.?

????????? Faculty shortages can be solved by engaging research scholars and visiting faculty but contract/ad hoc employment are a short-term solution.? Transparency in the selection committee mechanisms and Academic Performance Indicator calculations with equal emphasis on interviews and experience is integral.? Education outlay was hiked by 8 per cent in the Union Budget 2023-24, this needs further improvement.? For a future perspective, pedagogic reforms and synchronization of recruitment processes with best global practices are needed.? I urge the Government to look into the matter.? Thank you very much, Sir.??

(Ends)

records.subject: Regarding safety on Railways premises
records.SM_Text:
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA: Madam, on 25th June, 2023, a 34-year old woman, on her way to board a train to Chandigarh with her family, was electrocuted to death near Gate Number 1 of New Delhi Railway Station after coming into contact with an exposed live wire on an electricity pole at the Railway Station complex, in the midst of heavy rain.

Northern Railways claimed that the accident occurred due to an insulation failure and not because of any deficiency in the railways working system. Power distribution companies are responsible for electricity supply only to a certain portion of the New Delhi Railway Station, which excludes the leakages from the high mast lights that caused her death.

The incident took place on Railway property and the Railways should take responsibility for the maintenance of all electrical installations in its premises. But even after this sad tragedy, at various entry points, parking sites and exits of New Delhi Railway Station, exposed wires, shoddy and makeshift methods employed to manage open electric poles and junction boxes are witnessed. This negligence of Railway safety gains special importance post-Balasore accident.

I urge the Government to launch separate investigation into this death and immediately employ related prevention and safety measures. I also urge the Government and the Ministry of Railways to take prompt action and conduct a safety audit of all electric poles and electricity infrastructure to prevent any such incident in the future.

(Ends)

records.subject: Time consuming and prolonged organ donation procedures in the country
records.SM_Text:
Shri Tiruchi Siva : Organ donation in India is regulated by the 1994 Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act. The act aims to control the storage, and transplantation of organs and prevents any commercial dealings. At the same time, the National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (NOTTO) facilitates the procurement, allotment, and distribution of organs within India.

However, despite such legislations, there is a disparity between this colossal demand and low supply.

About 5 Iakh people in India die every year from causes that could have been prevented by organ transplants.

Organ donation rates in India stand at 0.86 per million population, a minuscule figure in comparison to countries like Spain which stands at 46.9 per million population. If Indias donation rates were to be improved to at least one donation per million deaths, it would satisfy the countrys organ requirement.

Despite the convenient donor registration process wherein any person willing to donate his/her organs can do so by filling out the donor consent form, organ donation is associated with numerous difficulties, namely, lack of awareness, and the spiritual belief of life after death.

I urge, the Government of India to come together with NGOs, CSOs, and non-state stakeholders to not only spread awareness and dispel myths and apprehensions in the minds of the people regarding organ donation but also to simplify the rules for Cadaver Organ Donations and Transplantations, to save precious lives through timely intervention.

(Ends)

records.subject: Concern over Jan Prasar’s withdrawal from the collaboration with AIR on the occasion of the Public Broadcasting Day.
records.SM_Text:
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (Tamil Nadu): Sir, on November 12, 1947, Mahatma Gandhi addressed the Indian refugees camping in Kurukshetra through a live broadcast arranged by All India Radio. More than 50 years later, in 2001, this day was officially declared Public Service Broadcasting Day.

Since then, Jan Prasar, a civil society organization, had been collaborating with All India Radio to commemorate this day in Gandhis memory every year. However, this year, Jan Prasar withdrew from the collaboration. The reason is, every year, a new school performs at the celebration. This year, the school choir which was supposed to perform two songs at the broadcast was asked to drop one of them without the knowledge of the civil society partner. This song was Gandhijis favourite Christian hymn, Make me a Channel of Your Peace. Additionally, the reason cited by the All India Radio for not including the hymn in the broadcast was that since the hymn was in English and therefore, it could not be sung. It was instead replaced by the performance of the BSF Jazz band.

Moreover, since 2000, All India Radio has celebrated that day by organizing an outdoor function, replete with Gandhijis bhajans, and with people seated on the ground as Gandhiji would in his mass contact programme. This year, however, the programme was moved indoors into

the AlRs newly-constructed Rang Bhawan auditorium, where the hour-long programme was telecast live.

These shocking turn of events by All India Radio go against the values propagated by Gandhiji; the values that must be honoured for more generations to come. Thank you, Sir.

(Ends)

records.subject: DEMAND FOR BANNING ONLINE GAMES/GAMBLING
records.SM_Text:
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (TAMIL NADU): Sir, my Special Mention is on Ban on Online Games with stakes which lead to addiction.

Sir, several online games involving the use of real money as bets have come up in the last few years. And with this, there has also been a surge in addiction to these games and a rise in suicide cases due to losing of money by individuals, reaching up to lakhs of rupees.

Sir, in the last five years, 7 suicide cases have been reported where the primary reason was losing money in an online game. There have also been reports of individuals addicted to the game, adopting extreme measures to procure money to use as wagers online.

Sir, there is an urgent need to address this issue and bring in a strong legislation for banning such games which involve betting real money. Even if games like rummy and poker are declared as games of skill, the element of placing a wager turns them into games which can be highly addictive and have been proved to be so.

Sir, teenagers and adults are both equally affected by this and gambling being so readily available in the hands of teenagers is highly concerning.

Sir, the Tamil Nadu Government brought in an amending Act in 2021 to address the issue, which included a ban and also fine and imprisonment for both the users and gaming houses for such games. The State continues to take it forward, as such games cannot be left unregulated and free-to-use specially by teenagers, as addiction to them is not only resulting in heavy economic losses, but also loss of lives.

Sir, I urge the Government to take it seriously and ban online games throughout the country.

(Ends)

records.subject: DEMAND FOR ELIMINATING ANOMALIES IN DEFENCE DISABILITY PENSION OF JAWANS  (SOLDIERS) AND OFFICERS IN ARMED FORCES
records.SM_Text:
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (TAMIL NADU): Sir, there exists a wide gap in the disability pension to Armed forces across ranks. Jawans receive a much less amount than the officers. Till 1971, there existed no disparity in the pension. Even after the Fifth Pay Commission, the disparity was not as wide and the pension was decided on the basis of disability. Today, this pension is calculated on a disability percentage, as per the last pay drawn. This leads to a huge gap and the jawans end up getting a much lower amount for the same disability. Even in the case of different disabilities, an officer with a 30 per cent disability will end up getting more than a jawan with 100 per cent disability, due to the difference in their salaries. As per the recommendation made by the Pay Commission, Rs. 12,000 were recommended for sepoys and Rs. 27,000 for officers. But, according to sources, the actual pension was fixed at Rs. 9,300 for the sepoys and Rs. 67,500 for the officers, which is almost seven times more than that of the sepoys. The sepoys deserve an equal compensation for their services to the country and they should not struggle to maintain a decent standard of living due to financial constraints. I implore the Government to consider this matter on humanitarian grounds and adopt a system to ensure that the disability pension fall within the same bracket across the ranks to ensure fair disability pension disbursal.

(Ends)

records.subject: DEMAND FOR PROMOTION OF SIDDHA MEDICINE SYSTEM ACROSS COUNTRY
records.SM_Text:
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (TAMIL NADU): Sir, the term AYUSH is an acronym for six Indian medicine systems, Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy. But it has been observed that all these systems are not being promoted equally in the country. Siddha medicine is one of the oldest Indian medical systems originating from Tamils/Dravidians and other than medicines. It also focuses on lifestyle changes as catalyst for better health. However, this medical system is not being given equal importance relative to other systems like Ayurveda in the country. While Ayurveda has 414 colleges in India across States, homoeopathy has 248 colleges and Unani has 55 colleges, Siddha has only 13 in two States, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. There is also a dedicated budgetary allocation for Ayurveda, Homoeopathy and Unani under the budgetary allocation to Ministry of AYUSH with the Central Council of Research under the three systems having a total of Rs.663.64 crore, but there is no devoted allocation for Siddha medicine. Even in our Parliament, there are hospitals for Ayurveda, Homoeopathy and Unani but none for Siddha.

It is time that the Central Government takes cognizance of the issue and recognizes the Siddha medicine system on par with other systems and ensures steps for its promotion. It also requires increased allocation for research and development and for establishing more colleges, hospitals and centres across the country including the Parliament House Complex.

(Ends)
records.Ministry: Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH)

records.subject: DEMAND FOR REDUCING GAP IN DISABILITY PENSION OF SERVICEMEN ON RANK BASIS
records.SM_Text:
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (TAMIL NADU): Sir, there is a wide disparity in the Defence disability pensions paid to the servicemen of the country. The differentiation is on the basis of the posts held by the servicemen.

The Seventh Pay Commission recommended disability pensions of Rs. 12,000, Rs. 17,000 and Rs.27,000 for Personnel Below Officer Rank (PBOR), Junior Commissioned Officers (JCO) and Officers respectively for 100 per cent disability. While adopting these recommendations, the Government has increased the disability pension of Rs. 27,000 to Rs. 67,000 to Officers and that of lower rank servicemen has been set at a paltry sum of Rs. 9,200.

This has created a vast gap in the disability pension available to the servicemen of our country on the basis of rank. It is crucial to understand that rank has nothing to do with disability and therefore should not be the basis of lower or higher disability pension. Already, disabled lower rank servicemen are distressed due to this decision.

The goal of updating the disability element in the Defence pensions must be driven by an intent to reduce anomalies and gaps. However, the current gap is hurting individuals who have dedicated their lives to the country. I urge the Government to do the needful to reduce this gap in the disability pensions of servicemen on the basis of rank.

(Ends)

records.subject: NEED FOR ENHANCING ALLOCATION OF FUNDS FOR EDUCATION
records.SM_Text:
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (TAMIL NADU): Sir, after several years, the country?s education Budget has suffered a cut of 6 per cent. The Department of School Education has suffered a cut of Rs. 5,000 crores, while the Department of Higher Education has been allocated approximately Rs. 1,000 crores lesser than the last financial year.

We cannot overlook the academic loss to students during the Corona pandemic. The dropout rate was predicted to double in India in 2020 and the effect on girl students will be worse. Online classes have revealed the gaps in access to internet and technology. With worsening education scenario, there is a need for the Government to pay more attention to the growth of this sector. Students have committed suicide because of their inability to attend online classes. Instances of child marriage and girl students being forced out of formal education due to increasing economic difficulty during the pandemic have also been reported.

In such a situation, reducing Budget to education will backfire on the students of our country. The UN Secretary-General spoke of an ?education catastrophe? globally, the current Budget will exacerbate the catastrophe on our students.

The Government cut expenditure on Mid-Day Meal Scheme, a crucial reason many students from poor families continue to attend school, from Revised Estimates of Rs. 12,900 crores last year to Rs. 11,500 crores this year impacts a lot.

Overcoming academic loss and initiating efforts to bring students back to schools also requires a strong financial backbone.

Hence, I urge the Government to look into the paucity of resources to education as the financial year progresses.

(Ends)

records.subject: DEMAND FOR DRAFTING NATIONAL SUICIDE PREVENTION POLICY UNDER MENTAL HEALTH CARE ACT, 2017 TO STOP GROWING INCIDENTS OF SUICIDE IN INDIA
records.SM_Text:
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (TAMIL NADU): Sir, According to data by the National Crime Records Bureau between 2018 and 2019, the number of deaths by suicide increased by 3.4 per cent. In comparison, 1,29,887 suicides were reported in 2017 whereas 1,39,123 were reported in the year 2019; an increase of almost 10,000 suicides within two years.

A research study on suicides during the Covid-19 lockdown period from March 24 to May 3, 2020 found an increase of 67.7 per cent in the number of suicides reported by newspapers, as compared to 2019, for the same period of time.

The findings of the study point towards an increasing trend in suicides by employed, middle-aged and married men. However, it cannot be ascertained if it is a case due to the lack of availability of real-time data on suicide and attempted suicides.

The impact of the pandemic has been far-reaching and has caused widespread economic, social, and emotional distress, which are known risk factors influencing suicide rates. A multi-pronged strategy to improve issues of health, livelihood and development is crucial to improve overall quality of life, and, in turn, prevent suicides.

I urge the Minister of Health and Family Welfare to draft a National Suicide Prevention Policy, as mandated under the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017. Further, it is recommended that real-time data on deaths by suicides and attempted suicides be gathered or a National Suicide Registry be set up to strengthen suicide prevention efforts and reduce deaths by suicide and attempted suicides in India.

?(Ends)

records.subject: NEED FOR ADDRESSING INEQUALITIES IN ACCESS TO EDUCATION DURING PANDEMIC OWING TO DIGITAL DIVIDE
records.SM_Text:
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (TAMIL NADU): Sir, with cases on the rise, schools remain shut with children now being able to access education solely through digital means. This has resulted in vast disparities in access to education among children. A recently released survey by the NSO for 2017-18 indicates this. States with the highest access are a little above 50 per cent which is still low. Larger states such as Tamil Nadu had access below 20 per cent. This is worsened by the rural-urban divide with rural areas having even fewer connections. Because of the Pandemic, cash strapped States like Tamil Nadu, do not have sufficient resources to bridge the digital divide.

It was promised by the hon. Prime Minister that in a thousand days the digital divide will be bridged. Education policies earlier have suggested increased spending, with the current policy aiming at 6 per cent but previous spending by the Centre shows abysmal hope. Children who do not

have access to internet fall behind by a whole term giving undue advantage for private school students.

More than one in five Indians above 7 years still cannot read and write in any languages. In this background, the Centre must immediately take steps partnering with NGOs working in the field of education and technology to introduce schemes to address this digital divide. Moreover, Jammu and Kashmir having recently been given access to 4G internet in two areas on a trial basis, the pandemic will widen the gap further.

I urge the Government to take immediate measures as this is the need of the hour. Thank you, Sir.

(Ends)

records.subject: Facilities offered by AI to passengers
records.extent: Air India uplifts in-flight meals from reputed caterers who also cater to other international and domestic airlines. Surprise meal checks are carried out at caterer's premises to monitor uplift of meals with regard to quality, quantity, taste, presentation and eye appeal. Periodic Hygiene Audits are also being carried out at caterer's premises to improve the quality of meals.
